title.zh: 卷五十七 吳書十二 虞陸張駱陸吾朱傳
title.en: Volume 57: Book of Wu 12 - Biographies of Yu, Lu, Zhang, Luo, Lu, Wu, and Zhu
title.raw: 卷五十七 吳書十二 虞陸張駱陸吾朱傳 Volume 57: Book of Wu 12 - Biographies of Yu, Lu, Zhang, Luo, Lu, Wu, and Zhu

sentences.zh: 虞翻字仲翔，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Fan, courtesy name Zhongxiang, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan, styled Zhongxiang, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻少好学，有高气。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: In youth Fan loved learning and bore himself with lofty pride.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu records that as a young man Yu Fan loved scholarship and carried himself with uncommon elevation.

sentences.zh: 年十二，客有候其兄者，不过翻，翻追与书曰：“仆闻虎魄不取腐芥，磁石不受曲针，过而不存，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: At age twelve a guest came to call on his elder brother but passed by without stopping for Fan; Fan pursued him with a letter saying: "I have heard that amber does not pick up rotten mustard and the lodestone does not take a bent needle; to pass by and pay no heed—is that not fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve, a visitor called on his brother but snubbed Yu Fan; Fan sent a letter after him: "They say amber ignores rotten mustard and a lodestone spurns a crooked needle—a slight delivered and unnoticed sits ill with neither party."

sentences.zh: ”客得书奇之，由是见称。〉

translations.literal: When the guest received the letter he marveled at it, and from this Fan was praised.
translations.idiomatic: The guest read the note with admiration, and Fan's reputation began from that hour.

sentences.zh: 太守王朗命為功曹。

translations.literal: Administrator Wang Lang appointed him Clerk of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator Wang Lang named him Clerk of Merit.

sentences.zh: 孫策征會稽，翻時遭父喪，衰絰詣府門，朗欲就之，翻乃脫衰入見，勸朗避策。

translations.literal: Sun Ce campaigned against Kuaiji; Fan was then mourning his father and came to the administrator's gate in mourning dress with hemp cord. Lang wished to approach him, but Fan removed his mourning garments and entered to see him, urging Lang to avoid Ce.
translations.idiomatic: While Sun Ce was marching on Kuaiji, Yu Fan was in mourning for his father; he appeared at the yamen gate in sackcloth. Wang Lang meant to comfort him, but Fan stripped the mourning garb, went inside, and urged Lang to withdraw rather than face Ce.

sentences.zh: 朗不能用。

translations.literal: Lang could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Lang would not follow his counsel.

sentences.zh: 拒戰敗績，亡走浮海。

translations.literal: He resisted in battle and suffered defeat, then fled and went out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: He fought and was routed, then fled by ship onto the open sea.

sentences.zh: 翻追隨營護，到東部候官，候官長閉城不受，翻往說之，然後見納。

translations.literal: Fan followed to guard the camp; they reached Houguan in the eastern division. The chief of Houguan closed the city and would not receive them; Fan went and persuaded him, and only then were they admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan stayed with the column as escort until they reached Houguan in the eastern circuit; the county magistrate barred the gates until Fan talked him round and won them entry.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻始欲送朗到广陵，朗惑王方平记，言“疾来邀我，南岳相求”，故遂南行。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Fan had first wished to escort Lang to Guangling; Lang was misled by Wang Fangping's inscription, which said "Come swiftly and invite me; the Southern Marchmount seeks me," and therefore went south.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu adds that Fan first meant to see Wang Lang safely to Guangling, but Lang trusted an inscription attributed to Wang Fangping—"Hasten and summon me; the Southern Peak calls"—and turned his course southward instead.

sentences.zh: 既至候官，又欲投交州，翻谏朗曰：“此妄书耳，交州无南岳，安所投乎？

translations.literal: After reaching Houguan he wished again to flee to Jiaozhou. Fan remonstrated with Lang: "This is a false inscription; Jiaozhou has no Southern Marchmount—where would you go?
translations.idiomatic: At Houguan he planned to bolt for Jiaozhou; Fan warned him: "That text is nonsense—there is no Southern Marchmount in Jiaozhou; what harbor could such a sign point to?

sentences.zh: ”乃止。〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Lang gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 朗謂翻曰："卿有老母，可以還矣。"

translations.literal: Lang said to Fan: "You have an aged mother; you may return."
translations.idiomatic: Lang told him: "You have an old mother at home—you should go back."

sentences.zh: 〈翻别传曰：朗使翻见豫章太守华歆，图起义兵。

translations.literal: The Separate Biography of Fan states: Lang sent Fan to see Administrator Hua Xin of Yuzhang, plotting to raise troops in righteous revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan's separate biography says Wang Lang dispatched him to Yuzhang's Hua Xin to plan raising loyal troops.

sentences.zh: 翻未至豫章，闻孙策向会稽，翻乃还。

translations.literal: Before Fan reached Yuzhang he heard that Sun Ce was heading for Kuaiji, and Fan then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Yuzhang he learned Sun Ce was bearing down on Kuaiji and wheeled about.

sentences.zh: 会遭父丧，以臣使有节，不敢过家，星行追朗至候官。

translations.literal: It happened that he was in mourning for his father; as an envoy under orders he dared not pass his home, but traveled by night and overtook Lang at Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: His father had just died, yet as an accredited envoy he would not detour home; he marched nights until he caught Wang Lang at Houguan.

sentences.zh: 朗遣翻还，然后奔丧。

translations.literal: Lang sent Fan back, and only then did Fan go to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Lang released him to return, and only then could Fan observe the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 而传云孙策之来，翻衰绖诣府门，劝朗避策，则为大异。〉

translations.literal: Yet the biography says that when Ce came, Fan in mourning dress went to the gate and urged Lang to avoid Ce—this is a great discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: The main narrative, however, claims that when Ce approached, Fan appeared at the yamen in mourning bands urging Lang to yield—quite another story.

sentences.zh: 翻既歸，策覆命為功曹，待以交友之禮。

translations.literal: After Fan returned, Ce again appointed him Clerk of Merit and treated him with the courtesy due a friend.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fan was back, Sun Ce restored him as Clerk of Merit and courted him as an equal.

sentences.zh: 身詣翻第。

translations.literal: He went in person to Fan's residence.
translations.idiomatic: He called at Fan's house himself.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策书谓翻曰：“今日之事，当与卿共之，勿谓孙策作郡吏相待也。”〉

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce wrote to Fan: "Today's affair I must share with you; do not think Sun Ce means to treat you as a mere clerk of the commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan records Ce's letter: "What we face now we shoulder together—do not imagine I would handle you like any county clerk."

sentences.zh: 策好馳騁遊獵，翻諫曰："明府用烏集之眾，驅散附之士，皆得其死力，雖漢高帝不及也。

translations.literal: Ce loved to gallop about on hunts. Fan remonstrated: "My lord, with troops gathered like flocking crows and officers who came from scattered allegiance, has won their utmost devotion—even Emperor Gao of Han did not match that.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce loved the chase; Fan warned him: "You have welded stray levies and loose adherents into men who will die for you—Emperor Gao of Han never drew such fealty."

sentences.zh: 至於輕出微行，從官不暇嚴，吏卒常苦之。

translations.literal: As for lightly going out incognito, attendants have no time to stand guard in full form, and clerks and soldiers constantly suffer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these disguised outings leave escorts no chance to secure a perimeter, and your staff pay the price again and again.

sentences.zh: 夫君人者不重則不威，故曰龍魚服，困於豫且，白蛇自放，劉季害之，願少留意。

translations.literal: One who rules men, if not grave, lacks awe; hence it is said the dragon in fish's garb was trapped by Yu Ju, and the white snake went freely until Liu Ji harmed it—I pray you take some heed.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler without dignity commands no respect—think of the dragon mistaken for a fish and caught by Yu Ju, or the white serpent that Liu Ji cut down when it roamed unchecked. I beg a moment's attention."

sentences.zh: "策曰："君言是也，然時有所思，端坐悒悒，有裨諶草創之計，是以行耳。"

translations.literal: Ce said: "What you say is right; yet at times my thoughts wander, and sitting upright I am restless—as Bi Chen had plans for the founding hour, that is why I go out."
translations.idiomatic: Ce answered: "True enough—but sometimes brooding leaves me restless at my desk; like Bi Chen sketching the design of a new age, I ride to clear my head."

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：策讨山越，斩其渠帅，悉令左右分行逐贼，独骑与翻相得山中。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: When Ce campaigned against the mountain Yue, he beheaded their chieftains and ordered his followers to split up and pursue the bandits; alone on horseback he met Fan in the hills.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu tells how Ce, campaigning against the mountain Yue, executed their chiefs and sent his men fanning out after the remnant—while he alone, mounted, ran into Yu Fan on a forest trail.

sentences.zh: 翻问左右安在，策曰：“悉行逐贼。

translations.literal: Fan asked where his attendants were; Ce said: "They have all gone to chase the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Fan asked where his escort was; Ce replied, "All out hunting bandits."

sentences.zh: ”翻曰：“危事也！

translations.literal: Fan said: "This is a perilous affair!
translations.idiomatic: Fan exclaimed, "This is reckless!"

sentences.zh: ”令策下马：“此草深，卒有惊急，马不及萦策，但牵之，执弓矢以步。

translations.literal: He ordered Ce to dismount: "This grass is deep; if alarm strikes suddenly the horse cannot be coiled with reins—only lead it and carry bow and arrows on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He made Ce dismount: "The grass is tall—if something strikes, you cannot wheel the horse in time. Lead it by the bridle and go on foot with bow ready."

sentences.zh: 翻善用矛，请在前行。

translations.literal: Fan is skilled with the spear; he requests to go ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Fan handled a spear well and asked to lead.

sentences.zh: ”得平地，劝策乘马。

translations.literal: When they reached level ground he urged Ce to mount the horse.
translations.idiomatic: On open ground he urged Ce back into the saddle.

sentences.zh: 策曰：“卿无马奈何？

translations.literal: Ce said: "You have no horse—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Ce said, "And you have no mount—what then?"

sentences.zh: ”答曰：“翻能步行，日可二百里，自征讨以来，吏卒无及翻者，明府试跃马，翻能疏步随之。

translations.literal: He answered: "Fan can walk two hundred li in a day; since the campaigns began no clerk or soldier has kept pace with Fan. My lord, try spurring your horse—Fan can follow at a measured walk.
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered: "On foot I cover two hundred li a day—since these campaigns began none of your runners has matched me. Spur your horse as you will; I will keep up at an easy stride."

sentences.zh: ”行及大道，得一鼓吏，策取角自鸣之，部曲识声，小大皆出，遂从周旋，平定三郡。

translations.literal: When they reached the main road they found a drummer; Ce took the horn and blew it himself. His troops recognized the signal and all came out, great and small; they then maneuvered together and pacified three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On the highway they found a signal drummer; Ce seized the horn and blew the rally himself. His units knew the call and poured in; wheeling together they brought three commanderies to heel.

sentences.zh: 江表传曰：策讨黄祖，旋军欲过取豫章，特请翻语曰：“华子鱼自有名字，然非吾敌也。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: When Ce campaigned against Huang Zu, on the return march he wished to take Yuzhang by the way and specially summoned Fan, saying: "Hua Ziyu has a reputation of his own, yet he is no match for me.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan relates that after striking Huang Zu, Ce meant to swing through and seize Yuzhang; he called Fan aside: "Hua Ziyu counts for something in reputation, but he is not my equal."

sentences.zh: 加闻其战具甚少，若不开门让城，金鼓一震，不得无所伤害，卿便在前具宣孤意。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear his weapons and stores are very few; if he does not open the gates and yield the city, once drums and gongs sound there will inevitably be harm—you go ahead and fully declare my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Word is his materiel is thin; if he will not open the gates and yield, the first roll of drum and gong will mean bloodshed. Go before me and speak my mind plainly."

sentences.zh: ”翻即奉命辞行，径到郡，请被褠葛巾与

translations.literal: Fan thereupon took his orders and set out; he went straight to the commandery and asked to put on a lined jacket and hemp headcloth to meet
translations.idiomatic: Fan took his orders, rode straight to the seat, and asked leave to dress in a plain jacket and hemp kerchief for an audience with

translations.literal: (the enemy)
translations.idiomatic: (the opposing side)

sentences.zh: 相见，谓歆曰：“君自料名声之在海内，孰与鄙郡故王府君？

translations.literal: him in audience. He said to Xin: "Between yourself and our former Administrator Wang of this humble commandery, whose fame resounds within the seas—which is greater?
translations.idiomatic: Facing Hua Xin he asked, "Measured against our late Administrator Wang here, whose name carries farther across the realm—yours or his?"

sentences.zh: ”歆曰：“不及也。

translations.literal: Xin said: "I do not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin admitted, "I fall short."

sentences.zh: ”翻曰：“豫章资粮多少？

translations.literal: Fan said: "How much grain and fodder has Yuzhang?
translations.idiomatic: Fan pressed: "How stand Yuzhang's grain stores?"

sentences.zh: 器仗精否？

translations.literal: Are weapons and armor refined or not?
translations.idiomatic: Are arms and armor fit?

sentences.zh: 士民勇果孰与鄙郡？

translations.literal: Are soldiers and people as brave and resolute as those of our humble commandery?
translations.idiomatic: Do soldiers and civilians match ours in fight?

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“不如也。

translations.literal: Again he said: "They do not compare.
translations.idiomatic: Again Xin said they did not.

sentences.zh: ”翻曰：“讨逆将军智略超世，用兵如神，前走刘扬州，君所亲见，南定鄙郡，亦君所闻也。

translations.literal: Fan said: "The General Who Punishes Rebels surpasses the age in wit and stratagem and wields troops like a god; routing Liu the Inspector of Yangzhou—that you saw with your own eyes; securing our humble commandery to the south—you have heard of that too.
translations.idiomatic: Fan continued: "The General Who Punishes Rebels outthinks his generation and moves armies like spirits—you watched him drive off Liu the Yangzhou Inspector; you know how he pacified our southern commandery."

sentences.zh: 今欲守孤城，自料资粮，已知不足，不早为计，悔无及也。

translations.literal: Now you wish to hold an isolated city; counting your grain and fodder you already know they are insufficient; if you do not plan early, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: To cling to an isolated wall when your stores already fail the tally is folly—delay until tomorrow and remorse will arrive too late.

sentences.zh: 今大军已次椒丘，仆便还去，明日日中迎檄不到者，与君辞矣。

translations.literal: Now our great army has already halted at Jiaoqiu; I shall return at once—if by midday tomorrow your surrender dispatch does not arrive, I take leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: The host is camped at Jiaoqiu; I ride back now—if by noon tomorrow no surrender comes, consider our conference ended."

sentences.zh: ”翻既去，歆明旦出城，遣吏迎策。

translations.literal: After Fan left, Xin came out of the city at dawn and sent clerks to welcome Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had hardly gone when Xin appeared at dawn beyond the walls and sent officers to greet Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 策既定豫章，引军还吴，飨赐将士，计功行赏，谓翻曰：“孤昔再至寿春，见马日磾，及与中州士大夫会，语我东方人多才耳，但恨学问不博，语议之间，有所不及耳。

translations.literal: After Ce secured Yuzhang he led the army back to Wu, feasted and rewarded officers and men, and reckoned merit for grants of honor. He said to Fan: "Long ago I twice went to Shouchun and saw Ma Midi; when I met gentlemen of the central plain they told me men of the east had talent indeed, but regretted that learning was not broad and that in speech and debate something was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuzhang taken, Ce withdrew to Wu, feasted the army, and parcelled rewards by merit. He told Fan: "Twice I visited Shouchun and met Ma Midi; central-plain scholars assured me the east bred talent but sighed that our book learning ran shallow and our debate lacked polish."

sentences.zh: 孤意犹谓未耳。

translations.literal: My thought still considered it not so.
translations.idiomatic: I was not convinced they were right."

sentences.zh: 卿博学洽闻，故前欲令卿一诣许，交见朝士，以折中国妄语兒。

translations.literal: You are broadly learned and well informed; therefore I earlier wished to send you once to Xu to meet court scholars and refute the foolish talk of the central states.
translations.idiomatic: You are learned and widely read; I meant to send you once to Xu to match wits with court scholars and silence the sneering boys of the interior."

sentences.zh: 卿不原行，便使子纲；

translations.literal: You were unwilling to go, so I sent Zigang;
translations.idiomatic: You declined, so I dispatched Zigang instead;

sentences.zh: 恐子纲不能结兒辈舌也。

translations.literal: I fear Zigang cannot tie the tongues of those fellows.
translations.idiomatic: I doubt Zigang can tie those youngsters' tongues."

sentences.zh: ”翻曰：“翻是明府家宝，而以示人，人倘留之，则去明府良佐，故前不行耳。

translations.literal: Fan said: "Fan is my lord's treasure of the house; to display him to others—if men should detain him, my lord would lose a fine aide; therefore I did not go before.
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied: "I am treasure kept under your roof; parade me abroad and some court might keep me—you would lose an arm. That is why I stayed."

sentences.zh: ”策笑曰：“然。

translations.literal: Ce laughed and said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Ce laughed: "Fair enough."

sentences.zh: ”因曰：“孤有征讨事，未得还府，卿复以功曹为吾萧何，守会稽耳。

translations.literal: He added: "I have campaigning affairs and cannot yet return to headquarters; you shall again act as Clerk of Merit—my Xiao He—and guard Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Campaigning keeps me from headquarters—stay again as my Xiao He in Clerk of Merit guise and hold Kuaiji for me."

sentences.zh: ”后三日，便遣翻还郡。

translations.literal: Three days later he sent Fan back to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he sent Fan home to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为王、华二公於扰攘之时，抗猛锐之锋，俱非所能。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Messrs Wang and Hua in that time of turmoil, facing fierce and sharp foes, were both unequal to the task.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that neither Wang nor Hua, in that chaotic hour, could truly have stood against such razor-edged force.

sentences.zh: 歆之名德，实高於朗，而江表传述翻说华，云“海内名声，孰与於王”，此言非也。

translations.literal: Xin's fame and virtue were in truth higher than Lang's, yet the Jiangbiao zhuan's account of Fan persuading Hua says "whose fame within the seas compares with Wang's"—this statement is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin's moral stature exceeded Wang Lang's, yet the Jiangbiao zhuan quotes Fan asking whose renown matched Wang's—that line is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 然王公拒战，华逆请服，实由孙策初起，名微众寡，故王能举兵，岂武胜哉？

translations.literal: Yet Lord Wang fought in resistance while Hua submitted when approached—it truly arose because Ce had only just risen, his name slight and followers few, so Wang could raise troops; was it martial superiority?
translations.idiomatic: Wang fought while Hua yielded chiefly because Sun Ce was new, obscure, and thinly manned—Wang could afford resistance then; was that martial superiority?

sentences.zh: 策后威力转盛，势不可敌，华量力而止，非必用仲翔之说也。

translations.literal: Later Ce's might grew steadily until none could withstand him; Hua measured his strength and stopped—not necessarily because he adopted Zhongxiang's arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ce's power swelled past answering, Hua gauged his odds and quit—not necessarily because Zhongxiang's rhetoric swayed him.

sentences.zh: 若使易地而居，亦华战王服耳。

translations.literal: Had they exchanged places, it would still have been Hua fighting and Wang submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Had their situations been reversed, Hua would have stood siege while Wang sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 按吴历载翻谓歆曰：“窃闻明府与王府君齐名中州，海内所宗，虽在东垂，常怀瞻仰。

translations.literal: According to the Wu li, Fan said to Xin: "I have heard in private that my lord and Lord Wang are paired in fame in the central plain and are honored throughout the land; though we are on the eastern edge we ever look up in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu calendar quotes Fan telling Xin: "Word reaches even our coast that you and Administrator Wang were paired as luminaries of the interior—we gaze upward though we stand far east."

sentences.zh: ”歆答曰：“孤不如王会稽。

translations.literal: Xin answered: "I am not the equal of Wang of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xin answered, "I am no match for Wang of Kuaiji."

sentences.zh: ”翻复问：“不审豫章精兵，何如会稽？

translations.literal: Fan asked again: "May I ask how Yuzhang's picked troops compare with Kuaiji's?
translations.idiomatic: Fan asked further how Yuzhang's elite troops compared with Kuaiji's.

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“大不如也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Far inferior.
translations.idiomatic: The reply: "Much weaker."

sentences.zh: ”翻曰：“明府言不如王会稽，谦光之谭耳；

translations.literal: Fan said: "When my lord says you do not match Wang of Kuaiji, that is speech of modest brilliance;
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "Calling yourself beneath Wang of Kuaiji is gracious modesty;

sentences.zh: 精兵不如会稽，实如尊教。

translations.literal: that the picked troops do not match Kuaiji accords in truth with what you aver.
translations.idiomatic: but admitting your troops fall short of Kuaiji's—that rings true."

sentences.zh: ”因述孙策才略殊异，用兵之奇，歆乃答云当去。

translations.literal: He then described Ce's unusual talent and stratagem and the marvel of his use of troops; Xin thereupon answered that he would depart.
translations.idiomatic: He sketched Sun Ce's singular gifts and uncanny generalship until Xin conceded he would yield.

sentences.zh: 翻出，歆遣吏迎策。

translations.literal: When Fan went out, Xin sent clerks to welcome Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Fan withdrew; Xin sent officers to welcome Ce.

sentences.zh: 二说有不同，〔此说为胜也〕。〉

translations.literal: The two accounts differ; [this version is the better one].
translations.idiomatic: The sources diverge; this reading carries the stronger claim.

sentences.zh: 翻出為富春長。

translations.literal: Fan went out and became magistrate of Fuchun.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was then appointed magistrate of Fuchun.

sentences.zh: 策薨，諸長吏並欲出赴喪，翻曰："恐鄰縣山民或有奸變，遠委城郭，必致不虞。

translations.literal: When Ce died, all the senior officials wished to go out to attend the funeral; Fan said: "I fear that in neighboring counties mountain people may harbor treachery; to leave the walls far behind would invite the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: At Ce's death every chief official meant to ride to the mourning hall; Fan warned that hill folk in neighboring counties might turn traitor if the towns were left empty.

sentences.zh: "因留制服行喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon they remained to observe mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: They stayed in place and observed the rites in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 諸縣皆效之，鹹以安寧。

translations.literal: Every county followed suit, and all remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: Other counties copied the measure and kept the peace.

sentences.zh: 〈《吴书》曰：策薨，权统事。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: When Ce died, Quan took charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu records Ce's death and Sun Quan's assumption of command.

sentences.zh: 定武中郎将暠，策之从兄也，屯乌程，整帅吏士，欲取会稽。

translations.literal: General of the Household Who Fixes Martial Affairs Gao—Ce's elder cousin by the male line—was stationed at Wucheng; he marshaled clerks and soldiers intending to seize Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gao, General Who Fixes Martial Might and Ce's elder male-line cousin, camped at Wucheng, drilled officers and men, and aimed to wrest Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 会稽闻之，使民守城以俟嗣主之命，因令人告谕暠。

translations.literal: When Kuaiji heard of it, it had the people guard the city awaiting the heir's orders, and sent someone to announce this to Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji manned its walls pending the heir's word and sent envoys to reason with Gao.

sentences.zh: 《会稽典录》载翻说暠曰：“讨逆明府，不竟天年。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu records Fan persuading Gao: "The General Who Punishes Rebels, our enlightened lord, did not finish his Heaven-allotted years.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dianlu preserves Fan's appeal to Gao: "Our General Who Punishes Rebels left life unfinished.

sentences.zh: 今摄事统众，宜在孝廉，翻已与一郡吏士，婴城固守，必欲出一旦之命，为孝廉除害，惟执事图之。

translations.literal: Now one who holds office and commands the host ought to be Xiaolian; I have joined the clerks and soldiers of the whole commandery in binding the city and holding firm; if we must stake our lives in a single day to rid Xiaolian of harm—only you, sir, will decide.
translations.idiomatic: Authority now rests with the nominated heir; this commandery's officers and I have chained the gates—if we must spend every life in one dawn to shield him from you, weigh that, sir."

sentences.zh: ”於是暠退。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gao withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gao drew off.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：此二书所说策亡之时，翻犹为功曹，与本传不同。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: These two books say that when Ce died Fan was still Clerk of Merit, which differs from this standard biography.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes that both texts place Fan still as Clerk of Merit at Ce's death—at odds with this main biography.

sentences.zh: 後翻州舉茂才，漢召為侍御使，曹公為司空辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: Later the province nominated him as Flourishing Talent; the Han court summoned him as Palace Attendant; when Lord Cao was Minister of Works he summoned him—but Fan accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: The province later nominated him Flourishing Talent; Han summoned him as palace attendant; Cao Cao as Minister of Works called him up—Fan refused every appointment.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻闻曹公辟，曰：“盗跖欲以餘财污良家邪？

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: When Fan heard that Lord Cao had summoned him, he said: "Would Robber Zhi use leftover wealth to stain a good household?
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says that on hearing Cao Cao's summons Fan muttered, "Would Robber Zhi smear a decent house with stolen coin?

sentences.zh: ”遂拒不受。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore refused the summons outright.

sentences.zh: 翻與少府孔融書，並示以所著《易注》。

translations.literal: Fan wrote to Minister of the Household Kong Rong and showed him his commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Fan corresponded with Kong Rong, Minister of the Household, and sent his commentary on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 融答書曰："聞延陵之理樂，睹吾子之治《易》，乃知東南之美者，非徒會稽之竹箭也。

translations.literal: Rong replied: "Hearing of Yanling's ordering of music and seeing my friend's treatment of the Changes, I know that the excellence of the southeast is not only Kuaiji's bamboo arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Rong answered: "As Yanling ordered music, so you order the Changes—the southeast's glory is not mere Kuaiji bamboo."

sentences.zh: 又觀象雲物，察應寒溫，原其禍福，與神合契，可謂探賾窮通者也。

translations.literal: Again you observe images and clouds, discern responses of cold and warmth, trace their blessings and ills, and match the spirits in tally—one may call this plumbing the hidden and exhausting the way of understanding.
translations.idiomatic: You read sky-signs and weather-turn, trace fortune's roots until they tally heaven—work worthy of one who sounds the depths of fate."

sentences.zh: "會稽東部都尉張紘又與融書曰："虞仲翔前頗為論者所侵，美寶為質，雕摩益光，不足以損。"

translations.literal: Zhang Hong, Commandant of the Eastern Division of Kuaiji, also wrote to Rong: "Yu Zhongxiang has indeed been attacked by critics; a fine gem taken as pledge is only brighter for carving and polishing—not enough to harm it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong, eastern Kuaiji commandant, added in his own letter: "Critics have nicked Yu Zhongxiang; polish only brightens a pledged jewel—it cannot diminish him."

sentences.zh: 孫權以為騎都尉。

translations.literal: Sun Quan appointed him Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 翻數犯顏諫爭，權不能悅。

translations.literal: Fan repeatedly offended his sovereign's dignity with blunt remonstrance; Quan could not be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fan importuned Quan until the sovereign's patience frayed.

sentences.zh: 又性不協俗，多見謗毀，坐徙丹楊涇縣。

translations.literal: Moreover his nature did not harmonize with common ways; he was often slandered, and for his offense was banished to Jing county in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ill-suited to fashion, he drew slander and was sentenced to exile in Jing county, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙圖取關羽，稱疾還建業，以翻兼知醫術，請以自隨，亦欲因此令翻得釋也。

translations.literal: Lü Meng plotted to take Guan Yu; feigning illness he returned to Jianye. Because Fan also understood medicine, Meng asked that Fan accompany him, intending thereby to secure Fan's release as well.
translations.idiomatic: Plotting against Guan Yu, Lü Meng feigned sickness back in Jianye; knowing Fan practiced medicine, he asked Fan along—partly to win Fan's release from banishment.

sentences.zh: 後蒙舉軍西上，南郡太守麋芳開城出降。

translations.literal: Later when Meng led the whole army west, Administrator Mi Fang of Nan commandery opened the city and came out in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng marched west at full strength, Mi Fang, Nan commandery's administrator, opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 蒙未據郡城而作樂沙上。

translations.literal: Before Meng had occupied the commandery seat he held music on the sandbank.
translations.idiomatic: Before occupying the walled city Meng staged music on a river shoal.

sentences.zh: 翻渭蒙曰：“今區區一心者麋將軍也，城中之人豈可盡信，何不急入城持其管答乎？

translations.literal: Fan said to Meng: "For now only General Mi is of one mind with us; can everyone in the city be trusted? Why not hurry into the city and take hold of the keys and bolts?
translations.idiomatic: Fan told Meng: "Only General Mi stands wholly with us—can you trust every soul inside? Seize the granary keys and gate bars now."

sentences.zh: ”蒙即從之。

translations.literal: Meng immediately followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Meng obeyed at once.

sentences.zh: 時城中有伏計，賴翻謀不行。

translations.literal: At the time there was a plot ambushed in the city; thanks to Fan's counsel it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: A concealed scheme stirred inside the walls; Fan's counsel kept it stillborn.

sentences.zh: 關羽既敗，權使翻筮之，得兌下坎上，節，五爻變之臨，翻曰："不出二日，必當斷頭。

translations.literal: After Guan Yu was defeated, Quan had Fan divine by milfoil; he obtained hexagram Jie (constraint), lower trigram Dui upper Kan, the fifth line changing to Lin. Fan said: "Within two days at most he will lose his head.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan Yu's defeat Quan had Fan cast yarrow: hexagram Constraint with a moving fifth line toward Approach. Fan declared, "Within two days his neck will part."

sentences.zh: "果如翻言。

translations.literal: It turned out exactly as Fan said.
translations.idiomatic: Events matched his reading exactly.

sentences.zh: 權曰："卿不及伏羲，可與東方朔為比矣。"

translations.literal: Quan said: "You do not reach Fuxi; you may be compared to Dongfang Shuo."
translations.idiomatic: Quan said, "You fall short of Fuxi—but you may rank with Dongfang Shuo."

sentences.zh: 魏將于禁為羽所獲，繫在城中，權至釋之，請與相見。

translations.literal: Wei general Yu Jin was captured by Guan Yu and confined in the city; when Quan arrived he released him and asked to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei general Yu Jin, taken by Guan Yu and held inside the walls, was freed when Sun Quan arrived; Quan asked for an audience.

sentences.zh: 他日，權乘馬出，引禁並行，翻呵禁曰："爾降虜，何敢與吾君齊馬首乎！

translations.literal: Another day Quan rode out and drew Jin to ride alongside; Fan shouted at Jin: "You, captive who surrendered—how dare you align your horse's head with our lord's!
translations.idiomatic: Another day Quan rode with Jin beside him; Fan barked, "You who yielded as a prisoner—how dare you ride stirrup to stirrup with our sovereign!"

sentences.zh: "欲抗鞭擊禁，權呵止之。

translations.literal: He wished to raise his whip to strike Jin; Quan shouted and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan raised his whip to lash Jin; Quan shouted him down.

sentences.zh: 後權於樓船會群臣飲，禁聞樂流涕，翻又曰：“汝欲以偽求免邪？

translations.literal: Later when Quan feasted his ministers on a tower ship, Jin heard the music and wept; Fan again said: "Do you seek release through pretense?
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet aboard a tower ship, Jin wept at the music; Fan snapped, "Tears to win sympathy—is that the game?"

sentences.zh: ”權帳然不平。

translations.literal: Quan was resentful and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Quan flushed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：后权与魏和，欲遣禁还归北，翻复谏曰：“禁败数万众，身为降虏，又不能死。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Later Quan made peace with Wei and wished to send Jin back north; Fan again remonstrated: "Jin defeated armies counted in tens of thousands, became a surrendered captive himself, and could not die for honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu records that after peace with Wei Sun Quan meant to return Jin north; Fan argued again: "Jin broke hosts counted in myriads, then lived on as a prisoner instead of dying honorably."

sentences.zh: 北习军政，得禁必不如所规。

translations.literal: The north is practiced in military administration; gaining Jin will surely fall short of what you plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei trains for war as routine—Jin will not buy what you hope."

sentences.zh: 还之虽无所损，犹为放盗，不如斩以令三军，示为人臣有二心者。

translations.literal: To return him though without harm is still like releasing a robber; better behead him to command the three armies and show ministers who harbor two hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Sending him home costs little, yet it frees a bandit; better strike off his head before the host as a warning to any minister who keeps two masters."

sentences.zh: ”权不听。

translations.literal: Quan did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Quan would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 群臣送禁，翻谓禁曰：“卿勿谓吴无人，吾谋適不用耳。

translations.literal: When the ministers saw Jin off, Fan said to Jin: "Do not suppose Wu lacks men—only my counsel happened not to be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: As the courtiers escorted Jin away, Fan told him, "Do not mistake silence for emptiness—Wu simply ignored my advice."

sentences.zh: ”禁虽为翻所恶，然犹盛叹翻，魏文帝常为翻设虚坐。〉

translations.literal: Though Jin was despised by Fan, he still greatly praised Fan; Wei Wendi often set an empty seat for Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin loathed Fan yet praised him unstintingly; Wei Wendi kept an empty cushion set for Fan at court."

sentences.zh: 權既為吳王，歡宴之末。

translations.literal: After Quan became King of Wu, at the close of a joyous feast.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Quan had taken the title King of Wu, a banquet drew toward its close.

sentences.zh: 自起行酒，翻伏地陽醉，不持。

translations.literal: He personally rose to pass the wine; Fan lay prostrate feigning drunkenness and did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Quan himself circulated the cup; Fan sprawled on the floor pretending drunkenness and refused it.

sentences.zh: 權去，翻起坐。

translations.literal: When Quan left, Fan sat up.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan passed on, Fan sat bolt upright.

sentences.zh: 權於是大怒，手劍欲擊之，侍坐者莫不惶遽。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon was greatly angry, seized a sword and wished to strike him; none of those seated in attendance were not alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Quan erupted, sword in hand; every guest froze in terror.

sentences.zh: 惟大司農劉基起抱權諫曰："大王以三爵之後殺善士，雖翻有罪，天下孰知之?且大王以能容賢畜眾，故海內望風，今一朝棄之，可乎？

translations.literal: Only Minister of Agriculture Liu Ji rose and embraced Quan, remonstrating: "Great King, to kill a worthy man after three cups—though Fan has guilt, who under Heaven would know? Moreover the great king by capacity to embrace worthies and nurture the multitude makes all within the seas incline with the wind; now to cast him aside in one morning—is it fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Only Minister of Agriculture Liu Ji sprang up, caught Quan by the arms, and pleaded: "If you execute a good man after the third toast, who will believe Fan deserved it? You drew the realm by sheltering talent—would you scrap that renown in a single dawn?"

sentences.zh: "權曰："曹孟德尚殺孔文舉，孤於虞翻何有哉！

translations.literal: Quan said: "Cao Mengde still killed Kong Wenju—what is solitary Yu Fan to me!
translations.idiomatic: Quan snarled, "Cao Cao murdered Kong Rong—what is one Yu Fan to me?"

sentences.zh: "基曰："孟德輕害士人，天下非之。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Mengde lightly harmed scholars; all under Heaven condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered, "Cao Cao struck down scholars lightly and the world condemned him."

sentences.zh: 大王躬行德義，欲與堯、舜比隆，何得自喻於彼乎？

translations.literal: The great king personally practices virtue and righteousness and wishes to rival Yao and Shun in eminence—how can you compare yourself to him?
translations.idiomatic: You pattern yourself on Yao and Shun—how dare you measure yourself against him?"

sentences.zh: "翻由是得免。

translations.literal: Fan thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Fan lived because of it.

sentences.zh: 權因敕左右，自今酒後言殺，皆不得殺。

translations.literal: Quan therefore ordered those about him: from now on when after wine someone speaks of killing, none may kill.
translations.idiomatic: Quan then commanded his attendants never again to carry out death sentences uttered in wine.

sentences.zh: 翻常乘船行，與麋芳相逢，芳船上人多欲令翻自避，先驅曰：“避將軍船！

translations.literal: Fan often traveled by boat and met Mi Fang; many on Fang's boat wished Fan to yield of himself; the outrider said: "Give way to the general's boat!
translations.idiomatic: Fan was rowing when he met Mi Fang; Fang's crew demanded Fan clear the channel—the herald shouted, "Make way for the general!"

sentences.zh: ”翻厲聲曰："失忠與信，何以事君？

translations.literal: Fan said in a stern voice: "Having lost loyalty and faithfulness, how shall one serve a lord?
translations.idiomatic: Fan roared back, "Faithless to lord and ally—what right have you to the title of general?"

sentences.zh: 傾人二城，而稱將軍，可乎？

translations.literal: You betrayed two cities for another yet call yourself general—is it fitting?
translations.idiomatic: You surrendered two cities yet parade the rank—is that fitting?"

sentences.zh: "芳闔戶不應而遽避之。

translations.literal: Fang shut his door without answering and hastily yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Fang slammed his shutters and gave way in haste.

sentences.zh: 後翻乘車行，又經芳營勞，吏閉門，車不得過。

translations.literal: Later Fan rode in a carriage and again passed Fang's camp barrier; the clerks closed the gate and the carriage could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fan drove past Fang's camp gate; the guards barred it and blocked his carriage.

sentences.zh: 翻復怒曰："當閉反開。

translations.literal: Fan again angrily said: "What ought to be closed is instead open.
translations.idiomatic: Fan thundered, "Gates that should stay shut stand wide—

sentences.zh: 當開反閉。

translations.literal: What ought to be open is instead closed.
translations.idiomatic: gates that should admit you slam shut—

sentences.zh: 豈得事宜邪？

translations.literal: How can this accord with what is fitting?
translations.idiomatic: does any of this follow rule or sense?"

sentences.zh: "芳聞之，有慚色。

translations.literal: When Fang heard it, he showed shame.
translations.idiomatic: Fang colored with shame when he heard.

sentences.zh: 翻性疏直，數有酒失。

translations.literal: Fan's nature was blunt and straightforward; he often had lapses due to wine.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt by temper and often rash with wine, Fan wore Quan's patience thin.

sentences.zh: 權與張昭論及神仙，翻指昭曰："彼皆死人，而語神仙，世豈有仙人也！

translations.literal: Quan discussed immortals with Zhang Zhao; Fan pointed at Zhao and said: "Those men are all dead, yet they speak of immortals—can there be immortals in the world!
translations.idiomatic: Discussing transcendents with Zhang Zhao, Fan jabbed a finger at Zhao: "Every sage you cite lies under earth—yet you prattle of immortals!"

sentences.zh: "權積怒非一，遂徙翻交州。

translations.literal: Quan's accumulated anger was not once only; he therefore banished Fan to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Old resentments crested; Quan banished Fan to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 雖處罪放，而講學不倦，門徒常數百人。

translations.literal: Though suffering punishment and exile, he lectured tirelessly and disciples were often several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Even in exile he lectured without tiring; hundreds sat at his feet.

sentences.zh: 〈翻别传曰：权即尊号，翻因上书曰：“陛下膺明圣之德，体舜、禹之孝，历运当期，顺天济物。

translations.literal: The Separate Biography of Fan states: When Quan assumed the imperial style, Fan submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty embodies the virtue of enlightened sageliness and exemplifies the filial piety of Shun and Yu; the revolution's fortune meets its appointed season; you comply with Heaven and succor the myriad beings.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan's separate biography records that once Quan took the imperial title, Fan memorialized: "Your Majesty unites enlightened sage virtue with the filial patterns of Shun and Yu; the mandate's turn has come; you aid Heaven in nurturing all below."

sentences.zh: 奉承策命，臣独抃舞。

translations.literal: Receiving and honoring the mandate relayed from Ce, your servant alone claps his hands and dances.
translations.idiomatic: To uphold the charge handed down from Ce—your servant alone could leap for joy."

sentences.zh: 罪弃两绝，拜贺无阶，仰瞻宸极，且喜且悲。

translations.literal: Guilt and abandonment cut off on both sides; I have no tier by which to bow in congratulation; looking up to the pole star of the throne I am both glad and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off by crime and exile, I lack stairs to offer congratulations; I gaze toward the throne—half joy, half grief."

sentences.zh: 臣伏自刻省，命轻雀鼠，性輶毫釐，罪恶莫大，不容於诛，昊天罔极，全宥九载，退当念戮，频受生活，复偷视息。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly examines himself: his allotted span is lighter than sparrow or rat, his disposition lighter than a hair's breadth; his crimes are none greater and admit no room short of execution; August Heaven knows no limit and has wholly pardoned him nine years; in retirement he ought to await the axe yet repeatedly receives life, stealing another glimpse and breath.
translations.idiomatic: I weigh myself: my life weighs less than a sparrow's, my nature thinner than a silk thread; my guilt admits only death—yet boundless Heaven spared me nine years; though I deserve the block, life was granted again and again, and I linger still."

sentences.zh: 臣年耳顺，思咎忧愤，形容枯悴，发白齿落，虽未能死，自悼终没，不见宫阙百官之富，不睹皇舆金轩之饰，仰观巍巍众民之谣，傍听锺鼓侃然之乐，永陨海隅，弃骸绝域，不胜悲慕，逸豫大庆，悦以忘罪。”〉

translations.literal: Your servant's years have reached the "ear-attuned" age; brooding on fault he is anxious and indignant; his form is withered and haggard, his hair white and teeth fallen; though he has not yet died, he mourns his final passing—unable to see the richness of palace halls and myriad officials, unable to behold the golden chariot ornaments of the imperial equipage; looking up at the lofty strains sung by the multitude of people, listening beside to the joyful peel of bells and drums—forever to sink at the sea's edge, bones cast in the outer wastes—unable to bear grief and longing, yet in the great celebration drifting at ease, pleased enough to forget guilt."
translations.idiomatic: I am past sixty: shame and anger consume me; I am a ruin of a man, hair white and teeth gone—still breathing yet mourning the tomb I shall never quit the frontier to see the court's splendor or the imperial equipage; I hear only rumor of hymns and festival drums—doomed to end my bones by the ocean's rim. Grief chokes me, yet your ascent floods me with joy until guilt itself fades."

sentences.zh: 又為《老子》、《論語》、《國語》訓注，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: He also composed exegetical glosses on the Laozi, Analects, and Discourses of the States, all handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote gloss-commentaries on the Laozi, the Analects, and the Discourses of the States that have circulated ever since.

sentences.zh: 〈翻别传曰：翻初立易注，奏上曰：“臣闻六经之始，莫大阴阳，是以伏羲仰天县象，而建八卦，观变动六爻为六十四，以通神明，以类万物。

translations.literal: The Separate Biography of Fan states: When Fan first completed his Commentary on the Changes he memorialized: "Your servant has heard that at the inception of the six classics nothing surpasses yin and yang; thus Fuxi looked up at Heaven and suspended the images, establishing the eight trigrams; observing their transformations he set six lines per hexagram into sixty-four, to communicate with spirit luminaries and classify the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan's separate biography says that when he first finished his Changes commentary he submitted: "Among the roots of the Six Classics none outweigh yin and yang; Fuxi therefore hung Heaven's patterns aloft, fixed the eight trigrams, and from shifting lines spun out sixty-four hexagrams to speak with the gods and sort the ten thousand things."

sentences.zh: 臣高祖父故零陵太守光，少治孟氏易，曾祖父故平舆令成，缵述其业，至臣祖父凤为之最密。

translations.literal: Your servant's great-grandfather, the late Administrator Guang of Lingling, in youth studied the Meng school Changes; your servant's great-great-grandfather, the late Magistrate Cheng of Pingyu, continued and described that enterprise; down to your servant's grandfather Feng it became most precise.
translations.idiomatic: My great-grandfather Guang, once prefect of Lingling, mastered the Meng Changes in youth; my great-great-grandfather Cheng, once magistrate of Pingyu, carried the tradition forward; my grandfather Feng refined it furthest."

sentences.zh: 臣亡考故日南太守歆，受本於凤，最有旧书，世传其业，至臣五世。

translations.literal: Your servant's deceased father, the late Administrator Xin of Rinan, received the foundation from Feng and possessed the oldest manuscripts; generation after generation transmitted the enterprise down to your servant—five generations.
translations.idiomatic: My late father Xin, once prefect of Rinan, studied under Feng and kept the earliest exemplars; five generations have handed the craft to me."

sentences.zh: 前人通讲，多玩章句，虽有秘说，於经疏阔。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars lectured comprehensively yet mostly toyed with clause-and-sentence glosses; though they had secret explanations, these were loose toward the classic.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier exegetes lectured widely but lingered on petty glosses; secret readings drifted from the text itself."

sentences.zh: 臣生遇世乱，长於军旅，习经於枹鼓之间，讲论於戎马之上，蒙先师之说，依经立注。

translations.literal: Your servant was born into a troubled age and grew up amid armies; he studied the classics between drum and shield and debated atop war-horses; receiving the teachings of former masters, he relied on the classic to compose commentary.
translations.idiomatic: I came of age in chaos and learned the canon between drumbeats and saddlebows; trusting my teachers, I anchor every note in the received text."

sentences.zh: 又臣郡吏陈桃梦臣与道士相遇，放发被鹿裘，布易六爻，挠其三以饮臣，臣乞尽吞之。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant's commandery clerk Chen Tao dreamed that your servant met a Daoist adept, hair loose and clad in deerskin, who spread the Changes' six lines, twisted away three of them and offered them as drink; your servant begged to swallow them all.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery clerk Chen Tao dreamed I met a Daoist with loose hair and deerskin cloak who laid out the six lines, plucked three for me to drink; I asked to drain them all."

sentences.zh: 道士言易道在天，三爻足矣。

translations.literal: The Daoist said the Way of the Changes rests in Heaven—three lines suffice.
translations.idiomatic: The adept answered that Heaven's Changes need only three lines."

sentences.zh: 岂臣受命，应当知经！

translations.literal: Could it be that your servant received a mandate and ought to know the classic!
translations.idiomatic: Surely fate meant me to grasp the canon!"

sentences.zh: 所览诸家解不离流俗，义有不当实，辄悉改定，以就其正。

translations.literal: Among the explanations your servant has surveyed, none depart vulgar currents; where the sense is improper or unreal, he has wholly revised and settled them to hit what is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Every commentary I read wallowed in convention; wherever sense missed truth I rewrote until it squared with the classic."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：‘乾元用九而天下治。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "When Qian's primal yang employs the nine, all under Heaven is well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "When the Creative's ninefold yang moves, the realm finds order."

sentences.zh: ’圣人南面，盖取诸离，斯诚天子所宜协阴阳致麟凤之道矣。

translations.literal: "The sage faces south—surely he takes his pattern from Li—this is indeed the way the Son of Heaven ought to harmonize yin and yang and summon qilin and phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: The sage faces south as the trigram Clarity dictates—that is how the Son of Heaven aligns yin and yang and draws auspicious omens."

sentences.zh: 谨正书副上，惟不罪戾。

translations.literal: Respectfully I submit the fair copy for presentation—only let there be no offense.
translations.idiomatic: I enclose a clean copy and beg indulgence for presumption."

sentences.zh: ”翻又奏曰：“经之大者，莫过於易。

translations.literal: "Fan again memorialized: "Among the great classics none surpasses the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Fan submitted again: "No classic rivals the Changes."

sentences.zh: 自汉初以来，海内英才，其读易者，解之率少。

translations.literal: Since early Han, talents within the seas who read the Changes have on the whole produced few explanations.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han began, brilliant men who tackled the book have offered thin commentary."

sentences.zh: 至孝灵之际，颍川荀谞号为知易，臣得其注，有愈俗儒，至所说西南得朋，东北丧朋，颠倒反逆，了不可知。

translations.literal: By the era of Xiaoling, Xun Xu of Yingchuan was styled one who knew the Changes; your servant obtained his commentary—it surpasses vulgar scholars—but as for his explanation of "gaining companions in the southwest, losing companions in the northeast," it is inverted and reversed and utterly incomprehensible.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling Xun Xu of Yingchuan passed for an Changes master; I have his gloss—it bests pedants—yet his reading of "friends in the southwest, loss in the northeast" flips sense entirely."

sentences.zh: 孔子叹易曰：‘知变化之道者，其知神之所为乎！

translations.literal: Confucius sighed over the Changes: "He who knows the way of transformation—does he not know what spirit does!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius marveled, "Who grasps change knows the work of spirits!"

sentences.zh: ’以美大衍四象之作，而上为章首，尤可怪笑。

translations.literal: " thereby praising the making of the Great Expansion's four images, yet placing it at the head of a chapter is especially laughably strange.
translations.idiomatic: —praising the Great Expansion's four emblems—yet opening a chapter with that line is absurd."

sentences.zh: 又南郡太守马融，名有俊才，其所解释，复不及谞。

translations.literal: Moreover Administrator Ma Rong of Nan commandery, famed as possessing outstanding talent—his explanations again fall short of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Nan commandery's Ma Rong, for all his reputation, still trails Xun Xu."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰‘可与共学，未可与適道’，岂不其然！

translations.literal: Confucius said "One may study with him but not yet walk the Way with him"—is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said you may study together yet not share the Way—was he not right?"

sentences.zh: 若乃北海郑玄，南阳宋忠，虽各立注，忠小差玄而皆未得其门，难以示世。

translations.literal: As for Zheng Xuan of Beihai and Song Zhong of Nanyang, though each set down commentary, Zhong is slightly short of Xuan, yet neither has found the gate—hard to display to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Beihai's Zheng Xuan and Nanyang's Song Zhong both annotated the text; Song lags Zheng slightly, yet neither found the doorway—unfit for public teaching."

sentences.zh: ”又奏郑玄解尚书违失事目：“臣闻周公制礼以辨上下，孔子曰‘有君臣然后有上下，有上下然后礼义有所错’，是故尊君卑臣，礼之大司也。

translations.literal: "He further memorialized errors in Zheng Xuan's Documents glosses under these heads: "Your servant has heard that the Duke of Zhou instituted ritual to distinguish high from low; Confucius said 'Only when there are lord and minister are there high and low; only when there are high and low can ritual and righteousness find their placement'—therefore honoring the lord and demeaning ministers is the great controller of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He added a catalogue of Zheng Xuan's mistakes on the Documents: "The Duke of Zhou framed rites to separate superior from inferior; Confucius said lord and minister precede order, and order precedes ritual—exalting the ruler and humbling ministers is ritual's backbone."

sentences.zh: 伏见故徵士北海郑玄所注尚书，以顾命康王执瑁，古‘月’似‘同’，从误作‘同’，既不觉定，复训为杯，谓之酒杯；

translations.literal: Your servant has seen the Documents annotated by the late Summoned Scholar Zheng Xuan of Beihai: at "Kang Wang holds the mao jade" in the Testamentary Charge the ancient character for "moon" resembled "same," and following error it was written as "same"; having failed to fix it, he glossed it as a cup, calling it a wine cup;
translations.idiomatic: On the Testamentary Charge passage where Kang Wang holds the mao ornament, Zheng mistook an archaic "moon" graph for "same," copied it wrong, never corrected it, and glossed the mao as a drinking cup;

sentences.zh: 成王疾困凭几，洮颒为濯，以为澣衣成事，‘洮’字虚更作‘濯’，以从其非；

translations.literal: when King Cheng was gravely ill leaning on the armrest, taohui for washing face he glossed as zhuo and took it as rinsing clothes for the completed rite; the character "tao" was groundlessly altered to "zhuo" to follow that mistake;
translations.idiomatic: when King Cheng lay dying against the bench he misread ritual face-washing as laundering garments, gratuitously rewriting "tao" as "zhuo" to suit the error;

sentences.zh: 又古大篆‘丱’字读当为‘柳’，古‘柳’‘丱’同字，而以为昧；

translations.literal: moreover in great-seal script the character guan should be read as liu; ancient "liu" and "guan" were the same graph, yet he took it as mei;
translations.idiomatic: in large seal script the character guan should be read liu; ancient "liu" and "guan" were one graph—yet Zheng glossed it as "dark";

sentences.zh: ‘分北三苗’，‘北’古‘别’字，又训北，言北犹别也。

translations.literal: "Divide the San Miao to the north"—"bei" is the ancient character for "bie," yet he glosses "north," saying "north" still means "separate."
translations.idiomatic: "Banish the San Miao north": bei is the old graph for "divide," yet Zheng glosses it as "north" as if north meant separate."

sentences.zh: 若此之类，诚可怪也。

translations.literal: Cases like these are truly strange.
translations.idiomatic: Such readings strain credulity."

sentences.zh: 玉人职曰天子执瑁以朝诸侯，谓之酒杯；

translations.literal: The Office of Jade Workers states the Son of Heaven holds the mao to audience the feudal lords—calling it a wine cup;
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Office says the Son of Heaven grasps the mao to meet lords—Zheng turns it into a goblet;

sentences.zh: 天子颒面，谓之澣衣；

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven washing his face he calls rinsing clothes;
translations.idiomatic: the royal face-wash becomes laundering robes;

sentences.zh: 古篆‘丱’字，反以为昧。

translations.literal: the great-seal "guan" graph he reads backward as mei.
translations.idiomatic: the seal-script guan he reads as gloom."

sentences.zh: 甚违不知盖阙之义。

translations.literal: This gravely violates the meaning of "not knowing, leave blank."
translations.idiomatic: That tramples the maxim to admit ignorance."

sentences.zh: 於此数事，误莫大焉，宜命学官定此三事。

translations.literal: On these several matters the error could not be greater; the academy officers ought to fix these three items.
translations.idiomatic: These three points demand correction by the academicians."

sentences.zh: 又马融训注亦以为同者大同天下，今经益‘金’就作‘铜’字，诂训言天子副玺，虽皆不得，犹愈於玄。

translations.literal: Moreover Ma Rong's gloss-commentary likewise takes "same" as meaning "great sameness under Heaven"; now the classic adds "metal" and writes "bronze"; his gloss speaks of the Son of Heaven's secondary seal—though neither hits the mark, it is still better than Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong likewise reads "same" as universal unity; received texts add "metal" and write "bronze"; his gloss on the secondary seal still misses the mark yet edges ahead of Zheng."

sentences.zh: 然此不定，臣没之后，而奋乎百世，虽世有知者，怀谦莫或奏正。

translations.literal: Yet if these remain unsettled, after your servant's death fervor may stir among a hundred generations; though the age may produce those who know, modesty will keep them from memorializing corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Left unsettled after my death, later scholars may guess yet stay silent out of false modesty.

sentences.zh: 又玄所注五经，违义尤甚者百六十七事，不可不正。

translations.literal: Moreover in the Five Classics annotated by Xuan, instances where meaning is violated are especially serious—one hundred sixty-seven matters—they cannot go uncorrected.
translations.idiomatic: Across Zheng's Five Classics I count one hundred sixty-seven grave violations—they cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 行乎学校，传乎将来，臣窃耻之。

translations.literal: Let them circulate in schools and transmit to posterity—your servant privately shames at it.
translations.idiomatic: To let this reach schools and sons' sons shames me."

sentences.zh: ”翻放弃南方，云“自恨疏节，骨体不媚，犯上获罪，当长没海隅，生无可与语，死以青蝇为吊客，使天下一人知己者，足以不恨。

translations.literal: "Banished to the south, Fan said: "I blame myself for blunt integrity and a frame unpleasing to superiors; offending above I earned guilt and must long sink by the sea's corner; while alive I have none to speak with, and in death green flies will be my mourners—if all under Heaven one man knows me, it is enough not to regret.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled southward he wrote, "My stiff spine and graceless bones offended the throne; I shall rot on this shore with none to talk to living and only blowflies for mourners dead—yet one true friend under Heaven would acquit my regret."

sentences.zh: ”以典籍自慰，依易设象，以占吉凶。

translations.literal: " He consoled himself with canonical texts, relied on the Changes to set images, and divined fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed himself with the canon, hung divinations on the hexagrams, and read good or ill from them."

sentences.zh: 又以宋氏解玄颇有缪错，更为立法，并著明杨、释宋以理其滞。

translations.literal: Moreover because Song's explanations of Xuan contained many slips, he again established methods and further composed Clarifying Yang and Explaining Song to unravel their blockages.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhong's reading of Zheng erred often; Fan framed new rules and wrote works to untangle Yang and Song.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：翻云“古大篆‘丱’字读当言‘柳’，古‘柳’‘丱’同字”，窃谓翻言为然。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: Fan said "In great-seal script the character guan ought to be read as liu; ancient 'liu' and 'guan' are the same character"—privately your servant holds Fan's statement correct.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that Fan's equation of the seal graphs guan and liu strikes him as sound.

sentences.zh: 故“刘”“留”“聊”“柳”同用此字，以从声故也，与日辰“卯”字字同音异。

translations.literal: Therefore "Liu," "Liu," "Liao," and "Liu" share this character by following the sound; it differs in pronunciation from the cyclical character "mao" though the graph looks alike.
translations.idiomatic: Hence surnames such as Liu, Liu, Liao, and Liu share that script by phonetic loan—not the cyclical stem-branch mao, though the graphs look alike.

sentences.zh: 然汉书王莽传论卯金刀，故以为日辰之“卯”，今未能详正。

translations.literal: Yet the Hanshu essay on Wang Mang discusses mao metal blade and therefore treats it as the cyclical "mao"; today one cannot detail and correct it fully.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanshu essay on Wang Mang's "mao metal blade" takes mao as the stem-branch character—a confusion I cannot fully untangle here.

sentences.zh: 然世多乱之，故翻所说云。

translations.literal: Yet the age mostly confuses them; therefore Fan spoke as he did.
translations.idiomatic: Common usage confuses them—hence Fan's warning."

sentences.zh: 荀谞，荀爽之别名。〉

translations.literal: Xun Xu is another name for Xun Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu is the alternate name of Xun Shuang."

sentences.zh: 初，山陰丁覽，太末徐陵，或在縣吏之中，或眾所未識，翻一見之，便與友善，終鹹顯名。

translations.literal: At first Ding Lan of Shanyin and Xu Ling of Taimo—some among county clerks, some unknown to the multitude—when Fan saw them once he befriended them, and in the end all became famous.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Lan of Shanyin and Xu Ling of Taimo—petty clerks or men the world had never heard of—won Yu Fan's friendship at a glance and rose to renown.

sentences.zh: 〈《会稽典录》曰：◎览字孝连，八岁而孤，家又单微，清身立行，用意不苟，推财从弟，以义让称。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu states: ◎ Lan, courtesy name Xiaolian, at eight sui was orphaned; his family was moreover humble; he purified himself and established conduct, his intentions never careless; he pushed wealth to a younger cousin and was praised for righteous yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dianlu notes Ding Lan, styled Xiaolian: orphaned at eight from a poor house, he kept scrupulous conduct, gave his inheritance to a cousin, and earned fame for yielding.

sentences.zh: 仕郡至功曹，守始平长。

translations.literal: He served the commandery up to Clerk of Merit and acted as magistrate of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Clerk of Merit and acting magistrate of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 为人精微絜净，门无杂宾。

translations.literal: As a man he was refined, subtle, and cleanly austere; no miscellaneous guests crossed his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Refined, punctilious, and austere, he admitted no casual callers.

sentences.zh: 孙权深贵待之，未及擢用，会病卒，甚见痛惜，殊其门户。

translations.literal: Sun Quan deeply prized and favored him; before he could promote him to office he died of illness; Quan greatly mourned and singled out his household for favor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan esteemed him highly but died before promoting him; Quan grieved deeply and honored his kin.

sentences.zh: 览子固，字子贱，本名密，避滕密，改作固。

translations.literal: Lan's son Gu, courtesy name Zijian, originally named Mi, changed to Gu to avoid Teng Mi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu, styled Zijian—born Mi—renamed Gu to avoid Teng Mi's name.

sentences.zh: 固在襁褓中，阚泽见而异之，曰：“此兒后必致公辅。

translations.literal: While Gu was still in swaddling Kan Ze saw him and marveled, saying: "This child will surely rise to duke or minister.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ze peered into his cradle and declared, "This boy will reach the highest councils."

sentences.zh: ”固少丧父，独与母居，家贫守约，色养致敬，族弟孤弱，与同寒温。

translations.literal: " Gu in youth lost his father and lived alone with his mother; the family was poor yet he kept restraint; in supporting her with gentle demeanor he showed utmost respect; a younger male cousin was orphaned and weak, and he shared cold and warmth with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu lost his father young and kept his mother in poverty yet filial ease; he sheltered a helpless cousin as his own."

sentences.zh: 翻与固同僚书曰：“丁子贱塞渊好德，堂构克举，野无遗薪，斯之为懿，其美优矣。

translations.literal: Fan wrote to a colleague serving with Gu: "Ding Zijian is deep as a spring and loves virtue; the hall's frame is well raised; in the wilds no stray firewood remains—such is his excellence; its beauty is supreme.
translations.idiomatic: Fan wrote a fellow official: "Ding Zijian is depth and virtue embodied; he raises the family hall without leaving kindling in the field—that is true grace."

sentences.zh: 令德之后，惟此君嘉耳。

translations.literal: Among heirs of fine virtue only this gentleman is praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Among sons of good stock none shines like him."

sentences.zh: ”历显位，孙休时固为左御史大夫，孙皓即位，迁司徒。

translations.literal: " He rose through eminent posts; under Sun Xiu he became Left Imperial Clerk; when Sun Hao ascended the throne he advanced to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to high office—Left Imperial Clerk under Sun Xiu, Minister of Education once Sun Hao ruled.

sentences.zh: 皓悖虐，固与陆凯、孟宗同心忧国，年七十六卒。

translations.literal: Hao was cruel and tyrannical; Gu with Lu Kai and Meng Zong shared one heart worrying for the state; he died at seventy-six sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao turned vicious, Gu joined Lu Kai and Meng Zong in loyal anxiety; he died at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 子弥，字钦远，仕晋，至梁州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Mi, courtesy name Qinyuan, served Jin and rose to Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi, styled Qinyuan, served Jin as Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孙潭，光禄大夫。

translations.literal: Grandson Tan, Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Tan became Household Grandee.

sentences.zh: ◎徐陵字元大，历三县长，所在著称，迁零陵太守。

translations.literal: ◎ Xu Ling, courtesy name Yuanda, served as magistrate of three counties and was renowned wherever posted; he advanced to Administrator of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Xu Ling, styled Yuanda, distinguished himself over three magistracies and became prefect of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 时朝廷俟以列卿之位，故翻书曰：“元大受上卿之遇，叔向在晋，未若於今。

translations.literal: At the time the court awaited him with the seat of a ranked minister; therefore Fan wrote: "Yuanda receives treatment worthy of a senior minister—even Shuxiang in Jin never knew such favor today.
translations.idiomatic: The court meant to give him ministerial rank; Fan wrote, "Yuanda gains honors Shuxiang never saw in Jin."

sentences.zh: ”其见重如此。

translations.literal: " Thus was he held in such esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard he commanded.

sentences.zh: 陵卒，僮客土田或见侵夺，骆统为陵家讼之，求与丁览、卜清等为比，权许焉。

translations.literal: When Ling died, retainers and farmland were sometimes seized; Luo Tong pleaded for Ling's household and asked that they be treated like Ding Lan, Bu Qing, and the rest—Quan approved.
translations.idiomatic: After Ling died, creditors preyed on his bondservants and fields; Luo Tong sued for his family and won Sun Quan's nod to match Ding Lan's precedent.

sentences.zh: 陵子平，字伯先，童龀知名，翻甚爱之，屡称叹焉。

translations.literal: Ling's son Ping, courtesy name Boxian, was renowned from childhood; Fan loved him deeply and often praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ping, styled Boxian, was a prodigy Yu Fan doted on and praised aloud.

sentences.zh: 诸葛恪为丹杨太守，讨山越，以平威重思虑，可与效力，请平为丞，稍迁武昌左部督，倾心接物，士卒皆为尽力。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke, as Administrator of Danyang, campaigned against the mountain Yue; deeming Ping grave in bearing and steady in counsel, fit to serve, he requested Ping as assistant magistrate; Ping was gradually promoted to Commander of the Left Wing at Wuchang, treated people with whole heart, and the soldiers all gave their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke, campaigning in Danyang, valued Ping's weight of character and took him as aide, then raised him to command Wu's left wing—where Ping won every rank and file heart.

sentences.zh: 初，平为恪从事，意甚薄，及恪辅政，待平益疏。

translations.literal: At first, when Ping served Ke as an aide, Ke thought little of him; once Ke became regent he grew colder toward Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Ke had once slighted Ping as a mere clerk; as chief minister he kept him at even greater distance.

sentences.zh: 恪被害，子建亡走，为平部曲所得，平使遣去，别为佗军所获。

translations.literal: When Ke was assassinated, his son Jian fled and was seized by Ping's retainers; Ping ordered him released, but another unit captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's son Jian ran into Ping's troops; Ping sent him on, only for another column to take him.

sentences.zh: 平两妇归宗，敬奉情过乎厚。

translations.literal: Ping's two wives returned to their natal clans; he honored them with devotion deeper than ordinary duty.
translations.idiomatic: He showed two estranged wives a generosity warmer than ritual required.

sentences.zh: 其行义敦笃，皆此类也。〉

translations.literal: His righteous conduct was earnest and steadfast—all of a piece with this.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity ran thick and true—every deed of this stamp.

sentences.zh: 在南十餘年，年七十卒。

translations.literal: In the south more than ten years, he died at seventy sui.
translations.idiomatic: He spent a dozen years in the far south and died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 〈《吴书》曰：翻虽在徙弃，心不忘国，常忧五谿宜讨，以辽东海绝，听人使来属，尚不足取，今去人财以求马，既非国利，又恐无获。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Though Fan lived in banishment his heart never left the state; he constantly urged that the five gorges of Wuxi deserved a campaign. With the Liaodong sea cut off, even hearing envoys come over to submit was hardly worth the trouble; now to squander our wealth buying horses serves neither the realm nor, he feared, would it succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says exile never dimmed Fan's patriotism—he pressed for action in Wuxi, dismissed Liaodong fealty across broken seas, and warned that trading treasure for horses helped nobody.

sentences.zh: 欲谏不敢，作表以示吕岱，岱不报，为爱憎所白，复徙苍梧猛陵。

translations.literal: He wished to remonstrate but dared not; he drafted a memorial and showed it to Lü Dai, who gave no answer; maligned by petty likes and dislikes, Fan was transferred again to Mengling in Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted advice for Lü Dai, heard nothing back, fell victim to slander, and was shifted deeper into Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 《江表传》曰：后权遣将士至辽东，於海中遭风，多所没失，权悔之，乃令曰：“昔赵简子称诸君之唯唯，不如周舍之谔谔。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Later Quan dispatched officers to Liaodong; they met storms at sea and many were lost; Quan regretted it and issued an order: "Long ago Zhao Jianzi said a chorus of yes-men is no match for Zhou She's blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan tells how failed Liaodong fleets moved Quan to cite Zhao Jianzi: flatterers cannot rival one honest Zhou She.

sentences.zh: 虞翻亮直，善於尽言，国之周舍也。

translations.literal: Yu Fan is candid and straight and excels at speaking his whole mind—he is our Zhou She.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan's blunt candor makes him Wu's Zhou She.

sentences.zh: 前使翻在此，此役不成。

translations.literal: Had Fan been there on that mission, the expedition would not have miscarried.
translations.idiomatic: With Fan at court that folly would never have sailed.

sentences.zh: ”促下问交州，翻若尚存者，给其人船，发遣还都；

translations.literal: " Hasten inquiry to Jiaozhou: if Fan still lives, furnish him a boat and escort him to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jiaozhou questioned at once—if Fan lived, send a ship to bring him home;

sentences.zh: 若以亡者，送丧还本郡，使兒子仕宦。

translations.literal: if he has died, send his coffin to his native commandery and appoint his sons to office.
translations.idiomatic: if he had died, return the coffin and ennoble his sons.

sentences.zh: 会翻已终。〉

translations.literal: It happened that Fan had already passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was already gone.

sentences.zh: 歸葬舊墓，妻子得還。

translations.literal: He was returned for burial in the old tomb; his wife and children could come back.
translations.idiomatic: His bones went to the family plot; wife and children were free to return.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：孙亮时，有山阴硃育，少好奇字，凡所特达，依体象类，造作异字千名以上。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu states: Under Sun Liang there was Zhu Yu of Shanyin who from youth loved rare graphs; wherever he grasped a form by analogy he coined distinct characters—more than a thousand names.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dianlu names Zhu Yu of Shanyin, a Sun Liang-era clerk who invented over a thousand variant characters by analogy.

sentences.zh: 仕郡门下书佐。

translations.literal: He served the commandery as a gate clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from gate clerk in the yamen.

sentences.zh: 太守濮阳兴正旦宴见掾吏，言次，问：“太守昔闻硃颍川问士於郑召公，韩吴郡问士於刘圣博，王景兴问士於虞仲翔，尝见郑、刘二答而未睹仲翔对也。

translations.literal: Administrator Puyang Xing, at the New Year's Day banquet seeing his clerks, remarked in conversation: "Long ago I heard how Zhu of Yingchuan solicited opinions on scholars from Zheng Zhaogong, how Han of Wu commandery asked Liu Shengbo, how Wang Jingxing questioned Yu Zhongxiang—I have seen Zheng's and Liu's answers but never Zhongxiang's reply.
translations.idiomatic: At the morning feast Puyang Xing recalled how earlier prefects had polled scholars—through Zhu of Yingchuan, Han of Wu, and Wang Jingxing—and admitted he had never seen Yu Fan's celebrated answer.

sentences.zh: 钦闻国贤，思睹盛美有日矣，书佐宁识之乎？

translations.literal: I have long wished to hear of the state's worthies and gaze on splendid accounts—is such material known to you, clerk?
translations.idiomatic: He confessed he had hungered after that lore—could the clerk supply it?

sentences.zh: ”育对曰：“往过习之。

translations.literal: " Yu replied: "In the past I studied it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered that he had memorized Fan's reply.

sentences.zh: 昔初平末年，王府君以渊妙之才，超迁临郡，思贤嘉善，乐采名俊，问功曹虞翻曰：‘闻玉出昆山，珠生南海，远方异域，各生珍宝。

translations.literal: At the close of the Chuping era Lord Wang, with abyss-deep talent, vaulted to administer the commandery; craving worthies and cherishing goodness he loved gathering famed talents, and asked Clerk Yu Fan: 'I hear jade issues from Kunshan and pearls from the southern sea—far lands each breed their treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Fan remembered how Administrator Wang, newly elevated, once asked him: 'Jade comes from Kun peaks and pearls from the southern sea—every quarter hoards its gems.

sentences.zh: 且曾闻士人叹美贵邦，旧多英俊，徒以远於京畿，含香未越耳。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard scholars sigh in praise of your noble commandery—of old it teemed with heroes, only because it lay far from the capital they never crossed the threshold bearing incense.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers praise your commandery's worthies—too distant from Luoyang to perfume the capital, yet rich in men.

sentences.zh: 功曹雅好博古，宁识其人邪？

translations.literal: Clerk, you delight in broad antiquity—do you know such persons?'
translations.idiomatic: You love old learning—can you name them?'

sentences.zh: ’翻对曰：‘夫会稽上应牵牛之宿，下当少阳之位，东渐巨海，西通五湖，南暢无垠，北渚浙江，南山攸居，实为州镇，昔禹会群臣，因以命之。

translations.literal: ' Fan answered: 'Kuaiji above answers to the Oxherd asterism, below matches the seat of Lesser Yang; east it washes the great sea, west it threads the Five Lakes, south it opens boundless marsh, north it fronts the Zhe River amid islets—southern hills shelter it and it truly anchors the province. Ancient Yu assembled his ministers here and heaven christened it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered: 'Kuaiji mirrors Oxherd above and Lesser Yang below—sea east, lakes west, limitless south, Zhe River north—the ground Yu chose when he rallied his lords.

sentences.zh: 山有金木鸟兽之殷，水有鱼盐珠蚌之饶，海岳精液，善生俊异，是以忠臣系踵，孝子连闾，下及贤女，靡不育焉。

translations.literal: ' Its hills hoard metal, timber, birds, and beasts; its waters yield fish, salt, pearls, and clams; sea vapor and mountain marrow gladly breed exceptional folk—hence loyal ministers tread heel on heel, filial sons crowd lane after lane, and down to worthy women none fail to thrive.
translations.idiomatic: Its hills and tides breed loyalty street by street—even women rise to renown.

sentences.zh: ’王府君笑曰：‘地势然矣，士女之名可悉闻乎？

translations.literal: ' Lord Wang smiled and said: 'The terrain is so—yet may I hear every name of gentlemen and ladies?'
translations.idiomatic: Wang smiled and pressed for names.

sentences.zh: ’翻对曰：‘不敢及远，略言其近者耳。

translations.literal: ' Fan answered: 'I dare not reach to antiquity—I will sketch only those near at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Fan begged leave to stay recent.

sentences.zh: 往者孝子句章董黯，尽心色养，丧致其哀，单身林野，鸟兽归怀，怨亲之辱，白日报雠，海内闻名，昭然光著。

translations.literal: Formerly the filial son Dong Dan of Gouzhang devoted heart and gentle demeanor to his parents, exhausted grief in mourning, dwelt alone in field and forest until birds and beasts warmed to him; he avenged kin insulted in broad daylight and his fame filled the realm—radiantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Dong Dan of Gouzhang—filial, wilderness-haunted, beast-taming avenger whose tale shook the empire.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫山阴陈嚣，渔则化盗，居则让邻，感侵退籓，遂成义里，摄养车妪，行足厉俗，自扬子云等上书荐之，粲然传世。

translations.literal: Grand Palace Grandee Chen Xiao of Shanyin—while fishing reformed bandits, at home yielded to neighbors, moved by encroachment withdrew his hedge and thereby forged Righteous Lane; he adopted an old woman who drove a cart—conduct enough to stiffen custom; from Yang Xiong upward memorials piled up recommending him, splendor handed down ages.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiao turned robbers into neighbors and adopted a cart-pushing crone—Yang Xiong among many sang his praise.

sentences.zh: 太尉山阴郑公，清亮质直，不畏强御。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zheng Gong of Shanyin—clear, bright, substantive, straight, unafraid of the mighty.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zheng faced bullies without flinching.

sentences.zh: 鲁相山阴锺离意，禀殊特之姿，孝家忠朝，宰县相国，所在遗惠，故取养有君子之謩，鲁国有丹书之信。

translations.literal: Lu Chancellor Zhongli Yi of Shanyin—gifted with singular bearing, filial at home and loyal at court, magistrate and minister—wherever he served kindness lingered; hence foster sons showed a gentleman's mold and Lu kept faith sealed in vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Yi governed Lu with mercy so deep it entered proverb.

sentences.zh: 及陈宫、费齐皆上契天心，功德治状，记在汉籍，有道山阴赵晔，徵士上虞王充，各洪才渊懿，学究道源，著书垂藻，骆驿百篇，释经传之宿疑，解当世之槃结，或上穷阴阳之奥秘，下摅人情之归极。

translations.literal: Chen Gong and Fei Qi likewise touched Heaven's heart; merit, virtue, and administrative record stand in Han registers. Summoned Zhao Ye of Shanyin and Summoned Wang Chong of Shangyu—each vast talent and abyssal virtue, learning that probes the Way's source, books trailing brilliance by the hundred, loosening knots in the classics and riddles of the age; some pierce yin-yang's secret depths, others lay bare human feeling's farthest shore.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged from Chen Gong to Wang Chong—Han historians carved their names; Zhao Ye and Wang Chong plumbed heaven and earth on the page.

sentences.zh: 交阯刺史上虞綦毋俊，拔济一郡，让爵土之封。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi Inspector Qimu Jun of Shangyu lifted an entire commandery from ruin and declined enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Qimu Jun saved Jiaozhi and refused a noble stake.

sentences.zh: 决曹掾上虞孟英，三世死义。

translations.literal: Clerk of Judgments Meng Ying of Shangyu—three generations died for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Three Meng Yings in a row chose death over dishonor.

sentences.zh: 主簿句章梁宏，功曹史餘姚驷勋，主簿句章郑云，皆敦终始之义，引罪免居。

translations.literal: Registrar Liang Hong of Gouzhang, Clerk of Merit Si Xun of Yuyao, Registrar Zheng Yun of Gouzhang—all upheld duty from first to last, citing fault to decline office.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hong, Si Xun, and Zheng Yun quit posts rather than stain their term.

sentences.zh: 门下督盗贼餘姚伍隆，鄮莫候反。

translations.literal: Gate Supervisor for Bandit Affairs Wu Long of Yuyao—Mo Hou rebelled in Mao county.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Long of Yuyao held the bandit portfolio when Mo Hou rose in Mao.

sentences.zh: 主簿任光，章安小吏黄他，身当白刃，济君於难。

translations.literal: Registrar Ren Guang and petty clerk Huang Ta of Zhang'an—each met naked blades to ransom a lord from peril.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Guang and Huang Ta bought their lord's life with their skin.

sentences.zh: 扬州从事句章王脩，委身授命，垂声来世。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Clerk Wang Xiu of Gouzhang—gave body and entrusted life, fame trailing later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu died so his lord might live—posterity remembers.

sentences.zh: 河内太守上虞魏少英，遭世屯蹇，忘家忧国，列在八俊，为世英彦。

translations.literal: Henei Administrator Wei Shaoying of Shangyu—met an age of hardship, forgot family and anguished for the state, counted among the Eight Worthies, a heroic model for the era.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaoying of the Eight Worthies chose the realm over hearth.

sentences.zh: 尚书乌伤杨乔，桓帝妻以公主，辞疾不纳。
