translations.literal: Minister Yang Qiao of Wushang—Emperor Huan would wed him to a princess; ple illness he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiao refused an imperial princess on grounds of sickness.

sentences.zh: 近故太尉上虞硃公，天姿聪亮，钦明神武，策无失谟，征无遗虑，是以天下义兵，思以为首。

translations.literal: The late Grand Commandant Zhu Gong of Shangyu—Heaven-granted keen brightness, revered clarity and martial spirit; stratagem never slipped, campaigns never lag—therefore righteous hosts across the realm wished him their chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gong united loyal armies when the Han flag frayed.

sentences.zh: 上虞女子曹娥，父溺江流，投水而死，立石碑纪，炳然著显。

translations.literal: The woman Cao E of Shangyu—when her father drowned in the river she cast herself into the current and died; a stone stele records her deed—brilliantly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Cao E leaped after her drowned father—the stone by the bank still tells it.

sentences.zh: ’王府君曰：‘是既然矣，颍川有巢、许之逸轨，吴有太伯之三让，贵郡虽士人纷纭，於此足矣。

translations.literal: ' Lord Wang said: 'That is settled—yet Yingchuan boasts the reclusion of Chao and Xu, Wu the triple yielding of Taibo; though your commandery swarms with scholars, those parallels suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang answered that Chaofu and Taibo already crowned Kuaiji's fame.

sentences.zh: ’翻对曰：‘故先言其近者耳，若乃引上世之事，及抗节之士，亦有其人。

translations.literal: ' Fan replied: 'Hence I began with near examples—should we summon high antiquity and men who hardened their integrity, there are such too.
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied that older marvels waited if Wang wished.

sentences.zh: 昔越王翳让位，逃于巫山之穴，越人薰而出之，斯非太伯之俦邪？

translations.literal: Formerly King Yi of Yue yielded the throne and fled to a cave on Witch Mountain; the Yue people smoked him out—is he not kin to Taibo?
translations.idiomatic: King Yi of Yue fled abdication into a cave—hardly less stubborn than Taibo.

sentences.zh: 且太伯外来之君，非其地人也。

translations.literal: Moreover Taibo was a lord from abroad, not a native of that soil.
translations.idiomatic: Taibo was an outsider in Wu by birth.

sentences.zh: 若以外来言之，则大禹亦巡於此而葬之矣。

translations.literal: If we speak of outsiders—the Great Yu likewise toured here and was buried here.
translations.idiomatic: Count Yu the exile—his grave lies in this soil too.

sentences.zh: 鄞大里黄公，絜己暴秦之世，高祖即阼，不能一致，惠帝恭让，出则济难。

translations.literal: Huang Gong of Great Village in Yin—purified himself under tyrannical Qin; when Gaozu took the throne Huang could not be summoned to court; Emperor Hui yielded respectfully, and when crisis came Huang emerged to save the hour.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gong hid from Qin and Han alike yet surfaced when the heir needed him.

sentences.zh: 徵士餘姚严遵，王莽数聘，抗节不行，光武中兴，然后俯就，矫手不拜，志陵云日。

translations.literal: Summoned Yan Zun of Yuyao—Wang Mang summoned him repeatedly but he stiffened his integrity and refused; only after Guangwu restored Han did he bend to office, twisting his wrist so he would not bow—ambition overtopped cloud and sun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zun defied Wang Mang, bowed only to Guangwu, and would not kneel.

sentences.zh: 皆著於传籍，较然彰明，岂如巢、许，流俗遗谭，不见经传者哉？

translations.literal: All stand in transmitted texts, luminously clear—how compare them to Chaofu and Xu You, vulgar hearsay absent from the classics?'
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds fill annals—not rumor like Chaofu lore.

sentences.zh: ’王府君笑曰：‘善哉话言也！

translations.literal: ' Lord Wang smiled: 'Excellent words indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Wang laughed—fine speech.

sentences.zh: 贤矣，非君不著。

translations.literal: Worthy indeed—without you they would not shine.
translations.idiomatic: None but Yu could have voiced it.

sentences.zh: 太守未之前闻也。

translations.literal: The Administrator had never heard this before.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect had never heard the catalogue.

sentences.zh: ’”濮阳府君曰：“御史所云，既闻其人，亚斯已下，书佐宁识之乎？

translations.literal: '" The Puyang Administrator said: "The Censor's list—having heard those names—below them, clerk, do you know any?"
translations.idiomatic: Puyang Xing pressed: who ranked beneath Fan's heroes?

sentences.zh: ”育曰：“瞻仰景行，敢不识之？

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Gazing on lofty conduct—how dare I not know?
translations.idiomatic: Yu bowed to virtue—how could he forget?

sentences.zh: 近者太守上虞陈业，絜身清行，志怀霜雪，贞亮之信，同操柳下，遭汉中微，委官弃禄，遁迹黟歙，以求其志，高邈妙踪，天下所闻，故

translations.literal: The recent Administrator Chen Ye of Shangyu—purified person and clear conduct, ambition like frost and snow, chaste brightness matching Liuxia's resolve; when Han faltered he resigned salary and hid in Yish's hills seeking his purpose—high and remote, his traces heard throughout the realm—therefore
translations.idiomatic: He named Chen Ye—spotless recluse of the Han collapse whose fame crossed provinces—therefore

sentences.zh: （桓文）

translations.literal: (Huan Wen)
translations.idiomatic: (Huan Wen)

sentences.zh: 〔桓文林〕遗之尺牍之书，比竟三高。

translations.literal: [Huan Wenlin] therefore sent him a letter spanning one chi, so that in the end he was classed with the Three Lofty Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Text variants name Huan Wen or Huan Wenlin as the man who wrote—posterity ranked Chen Ye with the Three Lofty Ones.

sentences.zh: 其聪明大略，忠直謇谔，则侍御史餘姚虞翻、偏将军乌伤骆统。

translations.literal: Those of keen wit, grand design, loyalty, blunt counsel—Attendant Censor Yu Fan of Yuyao and Lieutenant General Luo Tong of Wushang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan and Luo Tong stood for wit and blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其渊懿纯德，则太子少傅山阴阚泽，学通行茂，作帝师儒。

translations.literal: Those of deep virtue and pure integrity—Junior Tutor Kan Ze of Shanyin, learning thorough and conduct lush, who became the emperor's Confucian teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ze tutored the heir in classical breadth.

sentences.zh: 其雄姿武毅，立功当世，则后将军贺齐，勋成绩著。

translations.literal: Those of heroic bearing and martial resolution who forged merit in their age—General of the Rear He Qi, achievement blazing.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi's campaigns wrote themselves into Wu history.

sentences.zh: 其探极秘术，言合神明，则太史令上虞吴范。

translations.literal: Those who plumbed secret arts until speech matched the spirits—Grand Astrologer Wu Fan of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fan read heaven like an open book.

sentences.zh: 其文章之士，立言粲盛，则御史中丞句章任奕，鄱阳太守章安虞翔，各驰文檄，晔若春荣。

translations.literal: Those literary gentlemen whose words bloomed—Palace Assistant Censor Ren Yi of Gouzhang and Administrator Yu Xiang of Zhang'an—each drove prose and commands bright as spring blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yi and Yu Xiang lit the era with brush and edict.

sentences.zh: 处士

translations.literal: Recluses
translations.idiomatic: Among recluses

translations.literal: (Deng)
translations.idiomatic: (Deng)

sentences.zh: 卢叙，弟犯公宪，自杀乞代。

translations.literal: Lu Xu—his younger brother violated public statute; Lu killed himself begging to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xu died to ransom a guilty brother.

sentences.zh: 吴宁斯敦、山阴祁庚、上虞樊正，咸代父死罪。

translations.literal: Si Dun of Wuning, Qi Geng of Shanyin, and Fan Zheng of Shangyu—all bore capital punishment meant for their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Si Dun, Qi Geng, and Fan Zheng walked to the block for fathers' crimes.

sentences.zh: 其女则松阳柳硃、永宁

translations.literal: Among women—Liu Zhu of Songyang, of Yongning
translations.idiomatic: Among women—Liu Zhu of Songyang and another of Yongning

sentences.zh: （瞿素）

translations.literal: (Qu Su)
translations.idiomatic: (Qu Su)

sentences.zh: 〔翟素〕，或一醮守节，丧身不顾，或遭寇劫贼，死不亏行。

translations.literal: [Zhai Su]—some maintained widowhood after one wedding though death pressed them; some fell to brigands yet died without dishonoring womanly duty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Su (or Qu Su in some manuscripts) stands with widows who chose death over shame when steel crossed their path.

sentences.zh: 皆近世之事，尚在耳目。

translations.literal: All are matters of recent times still within hearing and sight.
translations.idiomatic: Living memory still holds these tales.

sentences.zh: ”府君曰：“皆海内之英也。

translations.literal: " The Administrator said: "They are all luminaries within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect murmured that Wu held the empire's best.

sentences.zh: 吾闻秦始皇二十五年，以吴越地为会稽郡，治吴。

translations.literal: I hear that in the twenty-fifth year of the First Emperor of Qin the lands of Wu and Yue became Kuaiji commandery with its seat at Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He asked when Qin turned Wu-Yue into Kuaiji seated at Wu.

sentences.zh: 汉封诸侯王，以何年复为郡，而分治於此？

translations.literal: The Han enfeoffed kings—what year did it again become a commandery and divide administration here?
translations.idiomatic: When did Han kings yield again to a direct prefect?

sentences.zh: ”育对曰：“刘贾为荆王，贾为英布所杀，又以刘濞为吴王。

translations.literal: " Yu answered: "Liu Jia became King of Jing; Jia was killed by Ying Bu; then Liu Pi became King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu traced Liu Jia's kingship, Ying Bu's murder, Liu Pi's crown.

sentences.zh: 景帝四年，濞反诛，乃复为郡，治於吴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Emperor Jing Pi rebelled and was executed; it again became a commandery administered from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's fourth year broke Pi and restored a Wu seat.

sentences.zh: 元鼎五年，除东越，因以其地为治，并属於此，而立东部都尉，后徙章安。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanding Eastern Yue was abolished; thereby that territory became the seat and was merged here, and an Eastern Division Commandant was established—later transferred to Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanding erased Eastern Yue and folded its lands under Kuaiji's eastern command.

sentences.zh: 阳朔元年，又徙治鄞，或有寇害，复徙句章。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yangshuo the seat moved again to Yin; when bandits harried it shifted to Gouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yangshuo moved the yamen to Yin, then Gouzhang under raid.

sentences.zh: 到永建四年，刘府君上书，浙江之北，以为吴郡，会稽还治山阴。

translations.literal: By Yongjian 4th year Administrator Liu memorialized: north of the Zhe River became Wu commandery; Kuaiji returned its seat to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjian split Zhe's north into Wu and brought Kuaiji home to Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 自永建四年岁在己巳，以至今年，积百二十九岁。

translations.literal: From Yongjian 4th year, cyclical jisi, down to this year counts one hundred twenty-nine years.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred twenty-nine years had passed since that resettlement.

sentences.zh: ”府君称善。

translations.literal: " The Administrator praised it as sound.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect applauded the chronology.

sentences.zh: 是岁，吴之太平三年，岁在丁丑。

translations.literal: That year was Wu's Taiping third year, cyclical dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: The dialogue fell in Wu Taiping 3, dingchou.

sentences.zh: 育后仕朝，常在台阁，为东观令，遥拜清河太守，加位侍中，推刺占射，文艺多通。〉

translations.literal: Yu later served at court, often in terrace archives; he became Director of the Eastern Observatory, was distantly appointed Administrator of Qinghe, advanced to Palace Attendant, and mastered divination, literary craft, and varied learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu rose to Dongguan director, Qinghe by patent, and palace consultant—master of omens and letters.

sentences.zh: 翻有十一子。

translations.literal: Fan had eleven sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan fathered eleven sons.

sentences.zh: 第四子汜最知名，永安初，從選曹朗為散騎中常侍，後為監軍使者，討扶嚴，病卒，

translations.literal: The fourth son, Si, was most renowned; at the start of Yong'an he went from Gentleman of the Selection Bureau to Regular Mounted Attendant; later he became Military Supervisor Envoy on the campaign against Fuyan and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-born Si stood tallest—promoted from Selection clerk to mounted attendant, then died leading troops against Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：汜字世洪，生南海，年十六，父卒，还乡里。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu states: Si, courtesy name Shihong, was born in Nanhai; at sixteen sui his father died and he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dianlu says Si, styled Shihong, was Nanhai-born and came home at sixteen when his father died.

sentences.zh: 孙綝废幼主，迎立琅邪王休。

translations.literal: Sun Lin deposed the young ruler and welcomed Prince Langye Wang Xiu to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin cast the boy emperor aside for Prince Langye's Sun Xiu.

sentences.zh: 休未至，綝欲入宫，图为不轨，召百官会议，皆惶怖失色，徒唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Before Xiu arrived Lin wished to enter the palace and plot treason; he summoned the hundred officials to council—all were terrified and bloodless, uttering only yes-yes.
translations.idiomatic: Lin meant to seize the palace before Xiu arrived; the bureaucrats could only nod, pale.

sentences.zh: 汜对曰：“明公为国伊周，处将相之位，擅废立之威，将上安宗庙，下惠百姓，大小踊跃，自以伊霍复见。

translations.literal: Si answered: "You, enlightened lord, stand as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou for the state; you hold general and minister rank and wield power to depose and enthrone—you will pacify the ancestral shrines above and bless the hundred surnames below; great and small leap with joy, each imagining Yi Yin and Huo Guang reborn.
translations.idiomatic: Si told Lin he played Yi Yin to the realm—why panic the court by rushing the harem?

sentences.zh: 今迎王未至，而欲入宫，如是，群下摇荡，众听疑惑，非所以永终忠孝，扬名后世也。

translations.literal: Now the king you welcome has not arrived yet you wish to enter the palace—in this way subordinates waver and the multitude listens in doubt—it is no way to secure loyalty and filial piety forever or lift your name for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the palace early would shake faith and stain his fame.

sentences.zh: ”綝不怿，竟立休。

translations.literal: " Lin was displeased but in the end enthroned Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lin sulked yet crowned Xiu.

sentences.zh: 休初即位，汜与贺邵、王蕃、薛莹俱为散骑中常侍。

translations.literal: When Xiu first ascended, Si served with He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as Regular Mounted Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu kept Si, He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as close attendants.

sentences.zh: 以讨扶严功拜交州刺史、冠军将军、餘姚侯，寻卒。〉

translations.literal: For merit in the Fuyan campaign he was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou, Champion General, and Marquis of Yuyao; soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyan won him Jiaozhou, the Champion baton, and Yuyan marquisate—then death.

sentences.zh: 汜弟忠，宜都太守。

translations.literal: Si's younger brother Zhong was Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zhong governed Yidu.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：忠字世方，翻第五子。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu states: Zhong, courtesy name Shifang, was Fan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dianlu gives Zhong as Fan's fifth son, styled Shifang.

sentences.zh: 贞固幹事，好识人物，造吴郡陆机於童龀之年，称上虞魏迁於无名之初，终皆远致，为著闻之士。

translations.literal: Chaste, firm, capable in affairs, skilled at recognizing men—he sought out Lu Ji of Wu commandery while still in childhood and praised Wei Qian of Shangyu before he had a name; both in the end rose far and became scholars of recorded fame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong spotted Lu Ji as a boy and Wei Qian before fame—both climbed high.

sentences.zh: 交同县王岐於孤宦之族，仕进先至宜都太守，忠乃代之。

translations.literal: He befriended Wang Qi of the same county from a clan of orphaned clerks; Wang advanced first to Administrator of Yidu, and Zhong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He bonded with clerk-born Wang Qi—Qi held Yidu first, Zhong followed.

sentences.zh: 晋征吴，忠与夷道监陆晏、晏弟中夏督景坚守不下，城溃被害。

translations.literal: When Jin campaigned against Wu, Zhong with Yidao intendant Lu Yan and Yan's younger brother Central Summer Commander Lu Jing held firm and would not yield; when the city broke they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong died defending Yidao beside Lu Yan and Lu Jing when Jin breached the walls.

sentences.zh: 忠子谭，字思奥。

translations.literal: Zhong's son Tan, courtesy name Si'ao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan styled Si'ao.

sentences.zh: 《晋阳秋》称谭清贞有检操，外如退弱，内坚正有胆幹。

translations.literal: The Jinyang qiu praises Tan as chaste and restrained with disciplined integrity—outwardly seeming yielding and weak, inwardly firm, upright, and bold in capacity.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinyang qiu calls Tan reserved yet steel inside—soft-spoken but unbending.

sentences.zh: 仕晋，历位内外，终於卫将军，追赠侍中左光禄大夫，开府仪同三司。〉

translations.literal: He served Jin, rose through inner and outer posts, ending as Defender-in-Chief—posthumously honored Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee with Office Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin he reached Defender-in-Chief and won posthumous ministerial glory.

sentences.zh: 聳，越騎校尉。

translations.literal: Song was Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song served as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 累遷廷尉，湘東、河間太守；

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Commandant of Justice, Administrator of Xiangdong and Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commandant of Justice and prefect of Xiangdong and Hejian;

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：耸字世龙，翻第六子也。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu states: Song, courtesy name Shilong, was Fan's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dianlu names Song as Fan's sixth son, styled Shilong.

sentences.zh: 清虚无欲，进退以礼，在吴历清官，入晋，除河间相，王素闻耸名，厚敬礼之。

translations.literal: Clear, empty of desire, advancing and retreating by ritual—in Wu he passed through pure offices; entering Jin he was appointed Chancellor of Hejian; Prince Su long hearing Song's name treated him with thick courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Ascetic and punctilious in Wu, he became Hejian chancellor under Jin; Prince Su honored his reputation.

sentences.zh: 耸抽引人物，务在幽隐孤陋之中。

translations.literal: Song drew forth men of affairs, striving for those hidden in obscurity, orphaned and lowly.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on lifting talent from hedgerows and hovels.

sentences.zh: 时王岐难耸，以高士所达，必合秀异，耸书与族子察曰：“世之取士，曾不招未齿於丘园，索良才於总猥，所誉依已成，所毁依已败，此吾所以叹息也。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Qi challenged Song: men of lofty repute reach only the outstandingly gifted; Song wrote his clansman Cha: "This age's recruitment never summons the toothless recluse from grove and garden nor seeks fine talent from the crude crowd; praise follows what is already made, slander tracks what is already ruined—that is why I sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi argued great names imply genius; Song answered his kinsman Cha that patronage chases winners and shuns unknowns—a vice worth mourning.

sentences.zh: ”耸疾俗丧祭无度，弟昺卒，祭以少牢，酒饭而已，当时族党并遵行之。〉

translations.literal: " Song loathed vulgar excess in mourning sacrifices; when younger brother Bing died he offered only the lesser beast sacrifice—wine and rice—and kinsmen alike followed the rule.
translations.idiomatic: He trimmed funeral feasts to wine and grain when Bing died, and kin copied him.

sentences.zh: 昺，廷尉尚書，濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Bing was Minister of Justice and Minister over the Masses, Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Bing rose to ministerial rank and governed Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昺字世文，翻第八子也。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu states: Bing, courtesy name Shiwen, was Fan's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dianlu records Bing, Fan's eighth son, styled Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 少有倜傥之志，仕吴黄门郎，以捷对见异，超拜尚书侍中。

translations.literal: In youth he cherished a free hero's ambition; serving Wu as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates he was singled out for quick repartee and vaulted to Palace Attendant Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wu valued his wit at the Yellow Gates and jumped him to palace minister.

sentences.zh: 晋军来伐，遣昺持节都督武昌已上诸军事，昺先上还节盖印绶，然后归顺。

translations.literal: When Jin's army came to strike he dispatched Bing with tally as Area Commander-in-Chief for all military affairs from Wuchang upward; Bing first returned tally, canopy, seals and ribbons, then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Facing invasion Bing surrendered credentials above Wuchang before yielding.

sentences.zh: 在济阴，抑强扶弱，甚著威风。〉

translations.literal: In Jiyin he checked the mighty and aided the weak—his martial awe stood renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiyin he humbled bullies and shielded commoners—justice visible on the street.

sentences.zh: 陸績字公紀，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Ji, courtesy name Gongji, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji, styled Gongji, hailed from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父康，漢末為廬江太守。

translations.literal: His father Kang was Administrator of Lujiang at the end of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kang governed Lujiang in Han's twilight.

sentences.zh: 〈谢承后汉书曰：康字季宁，少惇孝悌，勤脩操行，太守李肃察孝廉。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng's Later Han History states: Kang, courtesy name Jining, in youth was steeped in filial piety and fraternal duty, diligently cultivated conduct; Administrator Li Su nominated him Flourishing Talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng's Hou Hanshu says Kang, styled Jining, earned a Flourishing Talent nomination for filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 肃后坐事伏法，康敛尸送丧还颍川，行服，礼终，举茂才，历三郡太守，所在称治，后拜庐江太守。〉

translations.literal: Later Su was executed for an affair; Kang gathered the corpse and escorted the funeral to Yingchuan, observed mourning, finished the rites, was nominated Flourishing Talent, served as Administrator of three commanderies—each place praised his governance—and finally was appointed Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Su fell to the law Kang bore his body home, mourned fully, then rose through three prefectures to Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 績年六歲，於九江見袁術。

translations.literal: At six sui Ji met Yuan Shu on the Jiujiang road.
translations.idiomatic: Ji met Yuan Shu in Jiujiang at age six.

sentences.zh: 術出橘，績懷三枚，去，拜辭墮地，術謂曰：“陸郎作賓客而懷橘乎？

translations.literal: Shu produced oranges; Ji tucked three in his robe; leaving, he bowed in farewell and they fell to the ground; Shu said: "Young Lu, you pocket oranges while a guest?
translations.idiomatic: Shu offered oranges; six-year-old Ji hid three in his sleeve until they spilled at leave-taking—Shu teased him about stealing fruit.

sentences.zh: ”績跪答曰："欲歸遺母。

translations.literal: Ji knelt and answered: "I wished to take them home for my mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ji knelt and said he meant them for his mother.

sentences.zh: "術大奇之。

translations.literal: " Shu greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu stared in delight.

sentences.zh: 孫策在吳，張昭、張紘、秦松為上賓，共論四海未泰，須當用武治而平之，績年少末坐，遙大聲言曰："昔管夷吾相齊桓公，九合諸候，一匡天下，不用兵車。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce held Wu, Zhang Zhao, Zhang Hong, and Qin Song were chief guests; jointly debating that the four seas were not yet tranquil and arms must rule them, Ji—youngest, seated last—called loudly across the room: "Long ago Guan Zhong ministered Duke Huan of Qi—nine leagues of lords, one restoration under Heaven—without chariot warfare.
translations.idiomatic: At Ce's council on conquering the realm, boy Ji barked from the lowest seat that Guan Zhong unified Qi without war.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：'遠人不服，則修文德以來之。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'When distant folk do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them.'
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Confucius—win strangers with culture, not steel.

sentences.zh: '今論者不務道德懷取之術，而惟尚武，績雖童蒙，竊所未安也。

translations.literal: ' Those who debate today do not labor at virtue and winning hearts but honor force alone—though Ji is a child, privately he cannot rest easy.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded his youth yet insisted glorifying arms unsettled him.

sentences.zh: "昭等異焉。

translations.literal: " Zhao and the others wondered at him.
translations.idiomatic: The elders listened slack-jawed.

sentences.zh: 績容貌雄壯，博學多識，星歷算數無不該覽。

translations.literal: Ji's bearing was heroic and robust; broadly learned and widely informed—astronomy, calendars, reckoning—nothing he failed to survey.
translations.idiomatic: Strapping and encyclopedic, he mastered stars, calendars, and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 虞翻舊齒名盛，龐統荊州令士，年亦差長，皆與績友善。

translations.literal: Yu Fan by seniority bore famous weight; Pang Tong was Wu's celebrated scholar of Jingzhou; both were somewhat older—all befriended Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan and Pang Tong, his elders in fame, counted Ji friend.

sentences.zh: 孫權統事，闢為奏曹掾，以直道見憚，出為鬱林太守，加偏將軍，給兵二千人。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan took charge he summoned Ji as Clerk of Memorial Pillar—straight speaking made men wary—so he went out as Administrator of Yulin with concurrent Lieutenant General and an allotment of two thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Quan named him memorial clerk until blunt honesty exiled him to Yulin with rank and two thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 績既有躄疾，又意在儒雅，非其志也。

translations.literal: Ji already suffered lameness and his heart lay with scholar refinement—not his aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Lame and bookish, generalship never suited him.

sentences.zh: 雖有軍事，著述不廢，作《渾天圖》，注《易》釋《玄》，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: Though military duties pressed he never ceased writing—he composed the Chart of the Encompassing Heavens, annotated the Changes and expounded the Mystery—all handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Camp life never stopped his brush—his cosmograph and Change commentary survive.

sentences.zh: 豫自知亡日，乃為辭曰："有漢志士吳郡陸績，幼敦《詩》、《書》，長玩《禮》、《易》受命南征，遘疾遇厄，遭命不幸，嗚呼悲隔！

translations.literal: Yu foreknew his death-day and composed a elegy: "There was a Han loyalist, Lu Ji of Wu commandery—child steeped in Odes and Documents, grown adept at Rites and Changes—received mandate on southern campaign, met illness and hardship, Heaven's lot unkind—alas, sorrow sunders!
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the hour of death he drafted his lament—a scholar's epitaph for a Han heart broken on the Ling frontier.

sentences.zh: "又曰："從今已去，六十年之外，車同軌，書同文，恨不及見也。

translations.literal: " He added: "From now beyond sixty years carts will share gauge and script share form—I regret I shall not see it.
translations.idiomatic: He prophesied reunification within sixty years he would not live to witness.

sentences.zh: "年三十二卒。

translations.literal: " He died at thirty-two sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 長子宏，會稽南部都尉，次子睿，長水校尉。

translations.literal: Eldest son Hong, Commandant of South Kuaiji; second son Rui, Colonel of Long Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Hong commanded southern Kuaiji; Rui led the Long River corps.

sentences.zh: 〈绩於郁林所生女，名曰郁生，適张温弟白。

translations.literal: The daughter Ji fathered at Yulin was named Yusheng; she married Zhang Wen's younger brother Bai.
translations.idiomatic: His Yulin daughter Yusheng wed Zhang Bai, Zhang Wen's brother.

sentences.zh: 姚信集有表称之曰：“臣闻唐、虞之政，举善而教，旌德擢异，三王所先，是以忠臣烈士，显名国朝，淑妇贞女，表迹家闾。

translations.literal: Yao Xin's collected works preserve a memorial praising her: "Your servant has heard that Tang and Yu's government raised the good and instructed them, hoisted virtue and lifted the unusual—the Three Kings placed this first—therefore loyal ministers and steadfast martyrs shine in court annals, virtuous wives and chaste women leave traces in hamlet gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xin petitioned that Tang-Yu governance honored worthy women as much as loyal men.

sentences.zh: 盖所以阐崇化业，广殖清风，使苟有令性，幽明俱著，苟怀懿姿，士女同荣。

translations.literal: That widens transformative enterprise and plants pure wind abroad so whoever carries fine nature shows it in light or shade; whoever harbors excellence shares glory between gentlemen and ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Such praise steadies custom for men and women alike.

sentences.zh: 故王蠋建寒松之节而齐王表其里，义姑立殊绝之操而鲁侯高其门。

translations.literal: Hence Wang Zhuo set frost-pine integrity and the Qi king inscribed his lane; the righteous aunt forged unmatched resolve and the Lu marquis raised her gate.
translations.idiomatic: Classic exemplars—Wang Zhuo's lane, the Lu aunt's gate—prove the point.

sentences.zh: 臣切见故郁林太守陆绩女子郁生，少履贞特之行，幼立匪石之节，年始十三，適同郡张白。

translations.literal: Your servant has personally seen Yusheng, daughter of late Administrator Lu Ji of Yulin—she walked chaste singularity in youth, erected unyielding resolve like undriftable stone; at thirteen sui she married Bai of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial names Yusheng, Lu Ji's girl—betrothed at thirteen to Zhang Bai.

sentences.zh: 侍庙三月，妇礼未卒，白遭罹家祸，迁死异郡。

translations.literal: Three months attending the ancestral shrine—wife's rites unfinished—Bai suffered household calamity and died removed to another commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Three months into marriage Bai died afar in family disaster.

sentences.zh: 郁生抗声昭节，义形於色，冠盖交横，誓而不许，奉白姊妹嶮巇之中，蹈履水火，志怀霜雪，义心固於金石，体信贯於神明，送终以礼，邦士慕则。

translations.literal: Yusheng raised voice declaring her vow; righteousness shaped her face; coaches crossed pleading remarriage yet she swore refusal; she upheld Bai's sisters through peril, treading flood and fire—mind frost-bright, faith harder than metal or stone, spirit-trust piercing gods—she buried him by ritual so commandery gentlemen took her model.
translations.idiomatic: She refused every suitor, nursed Bai's sisters through ruin, and buried him—Wu's matrons took note.

sentences.zh: 臣闻昭德以行，显行以爵，苟非名爵，则劝善不严，故士之有诔，鲁人志其勇，巳妇见书，齐人哀其哭。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard virtue is proclaimed through conduct and conduct displayed through rank—without title or rank encouragement lacks sternness—therefore gentlemen receive dirges: Lu chronicled courage; the Ji wife entered texts and Qi mourned her cry.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial cites Lu dirges and Qi's weeping widow—honor needs a title.

sentences.zh: 乞蒙圣朝，斟酌前训，上开天聪，下垂坤厚，褒郁生以义姑之号，以厉两髦之节，则皇风穆暢，士女改视矣。”〉

translations.literal: Pray the sacred court weigh ancient precedent—open Heaven's hearing, extend Earth's generosity—award Yusheng the style Righteous Aunt to stiffen young widows' resolve—then royal wind flows serene and gentlemen and ladies revise their gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Yao begged the throne to name Yusheng Righteous Aunt and shame faint hearts.

sentences.zh: 張溫字惠恕，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wen, courtesy name Huishu, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen, styled Huishu, came from Wu.

sentences.zh: 父允，以輕財重士，名顯州郡，為孫權東曹掾。

translations.literal: His father Yun lightly prized wealth and heavily prized gentlemen—famed through provinces and commanderies—served Sun Quan as Clerk of the Eastern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Father Yun, famed for patronage, clerked Quan's eastern bureau.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: Yun died young.

sentences.zh: 溫少修節操，容貌奇偉。

translations.literal: Wen in youth cultivated integrity; his looks were singularly grand.
translations.idiomatic: Wen cultivated character and looked every inch a leader.

sentences.zh: 權聞之，以問公卿曰：“溫當今與誰為比？

translations.literal: Quan heard of him and asked his ministers: "With whom should Wen rank today?
translations.idiomatic: Quan asked the court Wen's peer.

sentences.zh: ”大

translations.literal: The compound honorific opens with the graph meaning "grand."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture

translations.literal: (Manuscript gloss supplying the graph read as "minister.")
translations.idiomatic: (the character si completing the title)

sentences.zh: 農劉基曰："可與全琮為輩。

translations.literal: Minister of Agriculture Liu Ji said: "He may stand in Quan Cong's generation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji replied that Wen ranked with Quan Cong."

sentences.zh: "太常顧雍曰："基未詳其為人也。

translations.literal: " Minister of Ceremonies Gu Yong said: "Ji has not scrutinized his person.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong cut in—Ji hardly knew Wen yet.

sentences.zh: 溫當今無輩。

translations.literal: Wen today has no peer.
translations.idiomatic: Wen has no peer now.

sentences.zh: "權曰："如是，張允不死也。

translations.literal: " Quan said: "If so, Zhang Yun did not die in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Quan cried that Yun's ghost might rest.

sentences.zh: "征到延見，文辭占對，觀者傾竦，權改容加禮。

translations.literal: " Summoned to Yan for audience—literary replies and extempore answers—spectators stood rigid; Quan changed expression and doubled courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan audience his eloquence staggered the hall; Quan bowed deeper.

sentences.zh: 罷出，張昭執其手曰："老夫托意，君宜明之。

translations.literal: Leaving, Zhang Zhao clasped his hand: "This old man trusts his intent—you should grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao whispered trust at parting.

sentences.zh: "拜議郎、選曹尚書，徙太子太傅，甚見信重。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Consultant, Minister of the Selection Bureau, transferred Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent—greatly trusted and weighted.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to Selection minister and heir tutor—Quan's favorite.

sentences.zh: 時年三十二，以輔義中郎將使蜀。

translations.literal: That year thirty-two sui, as General of the Household Establishing Righteousness he was sent to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-two he crossed to Shu as Establishing Righteousness general.

sentences.zh: 權謂溫曰："卿不宜遠出，恐諸葛孔明不知吾所以與曹氏通意，

translations.literal: Quan told Wen: "You ought not travel far—I fear Zhuge Liang may not grasp why I communicate intent with the Cao house
translations.idiomatic: Quan feared Kongming would misunderstand Wu's tie to Wei—

translations.literal: (Therefore)
translations.idiomatic: Therefore

sentences.zh: 故屈卿行。

translations.literal: I bend you to undertake this mission.
translations.idiomatic: he pressed Wen to accept the embassy.

sentences.zh: 若山越都除，便欲大構於蜀。

translations.literal: Once the mountain Yue are wholly cleared I intend great alliance with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue rebels fell he planned wide pact with Shu.

sentences.zh: 行人之義，受命不受辭也。

translations.literal: An envoy's duty accepts mandate, not wording.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys carry charge, not scripts.

sentences.zh: "溫對曰："臣入無腹心之規，出無專對之用，懼無張老延譽之功，又無子產陳事之效。

translations.literal: " Wen replied: "Entering I lack counsel from trusted belly; abroad I lack solo debate's skill—I fear neither Zhang Lao's spreading praise nor Zichan's exposition of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wen apologized for lacking Zhang Lao's fame or Zichan's tongue.

sentences.zh: 然諸葛亮達見計數，必知神慮屈申之宜，加受朝廷天覆之惠，推亮之心，必無疑貳。

translations.literal: Yet Zhuge Liang comprehends schemes and counts steps—surely he knows how divine considerations bend and stretch; moreover receiving Heaven-covering grace from court—inferring Liang's heart—surely no doubt or duplicity remains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhuge Liang would read Wu's sky-covering favor and harbor no suspicion.

sentences.zh: "溫至蜀，詣闕拜章曰：

translations.literal: " Wen reached Shu and ascended the palace steps to present memorial:
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu he mounted the stair with memorial in hand:

sentences.zh: 昔高宗以諒闇昌殷祚於再興，成王以幼沖隆周德於太平，功冒溥天，聲貫罔極。

translations.literal: Formerly Gaozong through mourning vigil made Yin's fortune flourish twice; King Cheng though infant magnified Zhou virtue into Great Peace—merit blankets all Heaven, fame pierces the limitless pole.
translations.idiomatic: He opened by praising Shang Gaozong and boy King Cheng—tottering thrones steadied by sage regents.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以聰明之姿，等契往古，總百揆於良佐，參列精這炳耀，遐邇望風，莫不欣賴。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty with keen intelligence matches antiquity's tally—ordering all affairs through worthy assistants—rank upon rank of refined brilliance—far and near incline with the wind—none fail to rejoice and rely.
translations.idiomatic: He hailed the Shu emperor's wit and bench of stars that drew the realm.

sentences.zh: 吳國勤任旅力，清澄江滸，願與有道平一宇內，委心協規，有如河水，軍事興煩，使役乏少，是以忍鄙倍之羞，使下臣溫通致情好。

translations.literal: Wu labors with soldier strength, clears the river shoals—wishes with the ordered Way to level all within the cosmos—hearts entrusted, plans aligned—like the Yellow River's flow—yet military tasks flare vexing; envoys run thin—therefore enduring shame of rustic bluntness—sent inferior minister Wen to convey cordial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu pled fatigue on every front yet stretched envoys to affirm alliance.

sentences.zh: 陛下敦祟禮義，未便恥忽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty honors ritual and righteousness—will not lightly disdain us.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed Shu would not scorn Wu's courtesy.

sentences.zh: 臣自

translations.literal: Your servant from
translations.idiomatic: From the moment your servant

translations.literal: (entered)
translations.idiomatic: (entered)

sentences.zh: 遠境，及即近郊，頻蒙勞來，恩詔輒加，以榮自懼，悚怛若驚。

translations.literal: distant territory down to the inner suburbs repeatedly received gracious inquiry—imperial edicts layered honors until awe and trembling seized me like fright.
translations.idiomatic: crossed the frontier into your suburbs every kindness fell until humble awe shook me like panic.

sentences.zh: 謹奉所□函書一封。

translations.literal: Respectfully presenting the sealed letter in one packet.
translations.idiomatic: He respectfully enclosed his prince's sealed dispatch.

sentences.zh: 蜀甚貴其才。

translations.literal: Shu prized his talent highly.
translations.idiomatic: Shu honored his gifts.

sentences.zh: 還，頃之，使入豫章部伍出兵，事業未究。

translations.literal: Returning, shortly afterward he was sent into Yuzhang to marshal troops—the undertaking unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Home again Quan posted him to muster Yuzhang troops—work cut short.

sentences.zh: 權既陰銜溫稱美蜀政，又嫌其聲名大盛，眾庶炫惑，恐終不為己用，思有以中傷之，會暨艷事起，遂因此發舉。

translations.literal: Quan secretly nursed grievance that Wen praised Shu government, moreover resented his swelling fame—the multitude dazzled—feared he would never serve himself—sought means to wound him—when Ji Yan's affair erupted he seized the opening.
translations.idiomatic: Quan envied Wen's Shu praise and towering name—Ji Yan's purge gave cover.

sentences.zh: 艷字子休，亦吳郡人也，溫引致之，以為選曹郎，至尚書。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Zixiu, also of Wu commandery—Wen drew him in as Gentleman of the Selection Bureau up to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yan—another Wu man Wen promoted to Selection minister.

sentences.zh: 艷性狷厲，好為清議，見時郎署混濁淆雜，多非其人，欲臧否區別，賢愚異貫。

translations.literal: Yan's nature was harsh and angular—loved pure critique—seeing court clerks turbid and mixed with many unfit men—he wished to praise and blame, separate worthy from fool along distinct tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Yan meant to cleanse the clerk corps with ruthless rankings.

sentences.zh: 彈射百僚，核選三署，率皆貶高就下，降損數等，其守故者十未能一，其居位貪鄙，志節污卑者，皆以為軍吏，置營府以處之。

translations.literal: He impeached the hundred officials, audited the Three Departments' selections—mostly demoting height to low and stripping several grades—those who kept old posts numbered fewer than one in ten; those greedy and base in office, low of aspiration and stain—all he made army clerks, housing them in camp bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered careers—demoting most clerks and drafting bottom feeders into camp duty.

sentences.zh: 而怨憤之聲積，浸潤之譖行矣。

translations.literal: Yet resentful voices piled up and soaking slander began to walk.
translations.idiomatic: Grudges mounted; poison memos flew.

sentences.zh: 競言艷及選曹郎徐彪，專用私情，愛憎不由公理。

translations.literal: All competed charging Yan and Selection Gentleman Xu Biao—employing private feeling—love and hate ignored public principle.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor branded Yan and Xu Biao partisan.

sentences.zh: 艷、彪皆坐自殺。

translations.literal: Yan and Biao both sat guilt and killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Both men suicide under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 溫宿與艷、彪同意，數交書疏，聞問往還，即罪溫。

translations.literal: Wen long shared Yan and Biao's intent—often exchanged letters—mutual inquiry shuttling—thereupon Wen was judged guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's letters to them damned him.

sentences.zh: 權幽之有司，下令曰：

translations.literal: Quan imprisoned him with judicial officers and issued order:
translations.idiomatic: Quan clapped him in jail and proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 昔令召張溫，虛己待之，既至顯授，有過舊臣，何圖兇丑，專挾異心！

translations.literal: Long ago I ordered Zhang Wen summoned—empty of self awaiting him—once arrived conspicuously invested—beyond old ministers—who guessed vicious ugliness would cling ulterior heart!
translations.idiomatic: Quan raged that Wen betrayed trust lavished on him.

sentences.zh: 昔暨艷父兄，附於惡逆，寡人無忌，故近而任之，欲觀艷何如。

translations.literal: Formerly Ji Yan's fathers and elder brothers attached to wicked rebellion—I harbored no taboo—drew him near and employed him—wishing to observe Yan's character.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled hiring Ji Yan despite kin guilt to test the man.

sentences.zh: 察其中問，形態果見。

translations.literal: Examining him midway—form and bearing indeed appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's colors showed soon enough.

sentences.zh: 而溫與之結連死生，艷所進退。

translations.literal: Yet Wen bonded with him through life and death; Yan's promotions and demotions
translations.idiomatic: Wen wagered life on Ji Yan's roster—every lift and fall

sentences.zh: 皆溫所為頭角，更相表裡，共為腹背，非溫之黨，即就疵瑕，為之生論。

translations.literal: were all Wen's leading horns—mutually outer and inner shell—shared belly and back—those not of Wen's faction—then picking flaws—fabricating discourse.
translations.idiomatic: answered to Wen alone; allies wore honor while outsiders faced forged scandal.

sentences.zh: 又前任溫董督三郡，指撝吏客及殘餘兵，時恐有事，欲令速歸，故授棨戟，獎以威柄。

translations.literal: Moreover previously Wen supervised three commanderies—directing clerk-retainers and remnant troops—at the time fearing incident wished him swift return—therefore invested halberd authority—rewarded with martial tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Quan reminded granting Wen halberd command to rush home reserves.

sentences.zh: 乃便到豫章，表討宿惡，寡人信受其言。

translations.literal: Instead he reached Yuzhang—memorializing to attack entrenched bandits—I trusted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Wen petitioned Yuzhang bandit hunts Quan funded.

sentences.zh: 特以繞帳、帳下、解煩兵五千人付之。

translations.literal: Specially assigned five thousand cord encirclement, curtain, and vexation-loosening troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand picked troops followed his banner.

sentences.zh: 後聞曹丕自出淮、泗，故豫敕溫有急便出。

translations.literal: Later hearing Cao Pi personally emerged at Huai and Si—therefore forewarned Wen—if urgent issue arises march at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi marched east Quan ordered Wen ready.

sentences.zh: 而溫悉內諸將，佈於深山，被命不至。

translations.literal: Yet Wen tucked all generals inside deep mountains—received order yet never arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Wen hid his host in hills and ignored mobilization.

sentences.zh: 賴丕自退。

translations.literal: Luckily Pi withdrew of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Pi retired without battle—luck alone.

sentences.zh: 不然，已往豈可深計，又殷禮者，本占候召，而溫先後乞將到蜀，扇揚異國，為之譚論。

translations.literal: Had it not been so—past fault—could it bear deep reckoning? Moreover Yin Li—originally summoned for astrology—yet Wen repeatedly begged officers sent to Shu—fanning foreign lands—staging debates for them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan lumped in Yin Li's Shu missions as Wen's foreign intrigue.

sentences.zh: 又禮之還，當親本職，而令守尚書戶曹郎，如此署置，在溫而已。

translations.literal: Moreover when Yin Li returned he ought to have resumed his proper office; instead he was ordered to hold Clerk of the Household Bureau of the Ministry—such placement rested with Wen alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Li should have reclaimed his old desk; Wen parked him in Household affairs—a patronage seat.

sentences.zh: 又溫語賈原，當薦卿作御史，語蔣康，當用卿代賈原，專衒賈國恩，為己形勢。

translations.literal: Moreover Wen told Jia Yuan he would recommend him Imperial Clerk, told Jiang Kang he would employ him to replace Jia Yuan—solely peddling state grace as personal leverage.
translations.idiomatic: He promised Jia Yuan the censorate and Jiang Kang Jia's chair—trading palace favors for faction.

sentences.zh: 揆其奸心，無所不為。

translations.literal: Weighing his treacherous heart—nothing he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Given that bent mind, no intrigue seemed beneath him.

sentences.zh: 不忍暴於市朝，今斥還本郡，以給廝吏。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to expose him in market and court—now dismiss him to native commandery to serve menial clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Quan spared him execution—sent him home as a scrub clerk.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼溫也，免罪為幸！

translations.literal: Alas, Wen—to escape guilt is fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Wen keeps his head—that passes for mercy.

sentences.zh: 將軍駱統表理溫曰：

translations.literal: General Luo Tong memorialized in Wen's defense, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong petitioned for Wen:

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下，天生明德，神啟聖心，招髦秀於四方，署俊乂於宮朝。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers: Your Highness—Heaven-born enlightened virtue, spirits-opened sage heart—summons fine talents from four quarters, installs excellence at palace dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He hailed Quan's divine patronage of scholars.

sentences.zh: 多士既受普篤之恩，張溫又蒙最隆之施。

translations.literal: Many gentlemen already received broadly generous grace—Zhang Wen moreover bore the loftiest largesse.
translations.idiomatic: Many owed Quan favor; Wen owed most.

sentences.zh: 而溫自招罪譴，孤負榮遇，念其如此，誠可悲疚。

translations.literal: Yet Wen himself drew condemnation—betrayed splendid meeting—thinking on this is truly grievous shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wen squandered favor—the thought pains Tong.

sentences.zh: 然臣周旋之間，為國觀聽，深知其狀，故密陳其理。

translations.literal: Yet your servant in circling attendance watched for the state—knows the facts deeply—therefore secretly sets forth the principle.
translations.idiomatic: As eyewitness he lays out truth.

sentences.zh: 溫實心無他情，事無逆跡，但年紀尚少，鎮重尚淺，而戴赫烈之寵，體卓偉之才，亢臧否之譚，效褒貶之議。

translations.literal: Wen in truth harbored no other intent—deeds showed no rebellious trace—but age still young, gravitas still shallow—while wearing fierce blazing favor, embodying towering talent, raising praise-and-blame talk, airing commendation-and-censure debate.
translations.idiomatic: Young, dazzled by fame, Wen trafficked in reputations—that stirred envy.

sentences.zh: 於是務勢者妒者寵，爭名者嫉其才，玄默者非其譚，瑕釁者諱其議，此臣下所當詳辨，明朝所當究察也，昔賈誼，至忠之臣也，漢文，大明之君也，然而絳、灌一言，賈誼遠退。

translations.literal: Thus power-seekers envied his favor, fame-seekers envied his talent, silent ones faulted his chatter, flawed ones dreaded his judgments—this ministers ought sift clearly and the enlightened court investigate thoroughly—long ago Jia Yi was utmost loyal minister, Han Wen utmost enlightened lord—yet one word from Zhou Bo and Guan Ying—Jia Yi withdrew far.
translations.idiomatic: Envy drove out Jia Yi despite Han Wendi's wisdom—slander works that way.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 疾之者深，譖之者巧也。

translations.literal: Those who hated him were deep; those who slandered him were clever.
translations.idiomatic: Malice ran deep; rumor wore silk gloves.

sentences.zh: 然而誤聞於天下，失彰於後世，故孔子曰：‘為君難，為臣不易’也。

translations.literal: Yet error reached all under Heaven—failure blazed posterity—therefore Confucius said: 'Hard it is to be lord; hard it is to be minister.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius knew rulers mishear—fame lies and lasts.

sentences.zh: 溫雖智非從橫，武非虓武，然其弘雅之素，英秀之德，文章之采，論議之辯，卓躒冠群，煒曄曜世，世人未有及之者也。

translations.literal: Though Wen's wit matched no alliance strategist nor martial prowess no roaring tiger—yet his breadth and elegance, heroic brilliance, literary color, debating eloquence—towering above the crowd, blazing through the age—none among contemporaries matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen lacked warrior fame yet outshone Wu in letters and debate.

sentences.zh: 故論溫才即可惜，言罪則可恕。

translations.literal: Therefore judging Wen's talent—it is pitiable to waste; speaking guilt—it may be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Talent scarce and fault overstated.

sentences.zh: 若忍威烈以赦盛德，有賢才以敦大業，固明朝之休光，四方之麗觀也。

translations.literal: If you curb awesome wrath to pardon splendid virtue—thereby cherish worthy talent to shore great enterprise—it surely becomes enlightened court's radiant glory and four quarters' splendid spectacle.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy would crown Quan's reign.

sentences.zh: 國家之於暨艷，不內之忌族，猶等之平民，是故先見用於朱治，次見舉於眾人，中見任於明朝，亦見交於溫也。

translations.literal: The state toward Ji Yan—did not enroll him among taboo clans—still ranked him with common folk—therefore first employed by Zhu Zhi, next raised by multitude, middle trusted by enlightened court, also befriended by Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan rose through Zhu Zhi and public notice—not a palace villain.

sentences.zh: 君臣之義，義之最重，朋友之交，交之最輕者也。

translations.literal: Lord-minister righteousness—among duties weightiest; friend acquaintance—among ties lightest.
translations.idiomatic: Court bonds outweigh private friendship.

sentences.zh: 國家不嫌於艷為最重之義，是以溫亦不嫌與艷為最輕之交也。

translations.literal: The state did not fault Yan for weightiest duty—therefore Wen may fault neither lightest friendship with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: If Wu tolerated Yan, Wen's letters were harmless.

sentences.zh: 時世寵之於上，溫竊親之於下也。

translations.literal: The age favored him above—Wen drew him close below.
translations.idiomatic: Court lifted Yan; Wen only mirrored.

sentences.zh: 夫宿惡之民，放逸山險，則為勁寇，將置平土，則為健兵，故溫念在欲取宿惡，以除勁寇之害，而增健兵之銳也。

translations.literal: Now hardened wicked folk—released to mountain peril become fierce bandits—settled on level ground become stout soldiers—therefore Wen's thought aimed to seize entrenched wickedness—to remove fierce bandit harm and sharpen sound troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's bandit hunt aimed to draft grit into the ranks.

sentences.zh: 但自錯落，功不副言。

translations.literal: Only himself disordered—achievement fell short of words.
translations.idiomatic: Plans tangled; results lagged boasts.

sentences.zh: 然計其送兵，以比許晏，數之多少，溫不減之。

translations.literal: Yet counting troops dispatched—compared to Xu Yan—whether more or fewer—Wen diminished nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He matched Xu Yan's levy numbers.

sentences.zh: 用之強羸，溫不下之。

translations.literal: In using strong and weak—Wen fell short of none.
translations.idiomatic: Troop quality matched precedent.

sentences.zh: 至於遲速，溫不後之，故得及秋冬之月，赴有警之期，不敢忘恩而遺力也。

translations.literal: As for speed—Wen lagged behind none—therefore reached autumn-winter months—met alarm's appointed season—dared not forget grace and slack effort.
translations.idiomatic: He hit the autumn timeline despite hurry.

sentences.zh: 溫之到蜀，共譽殷禮，雖臣無境外之交，亦有可原也。

translations.literal: Wen's reaching Shu—jointly praised Yin Li—though ministers ought have no dealings beyond borders—still something forgivable.
translations.idiomatic: Praising Yin Li on embassy matched ritual allowance.

sentences.zh: 境外之交，謂無君命而私相從，非國事而陰相聞者也。

translations.literal: Dealings beyond borders mean lacking lordly mandate yet privately following—not state business yet secretly informing.
translations.idiomatic: Private intrigue differs from accredited talk.

sentences.zh: 若以命行，既修君好，因敘己情，亦使臣之道也。

translations.literal: If acting under mandate—cultivating lordly goodwill—thereby narrating personal sentiment—that too is minister's way.
translations.idiomatic: Mandated envoys may trade courtesy.

sentences.zh: 故孔子使鄰國，則有私覿之禮。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius sent to neighboring states—there existed protocol for private audience.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius allowed private audiences abroad.

sentences.zh: 季子聘諸夏，亦有燕譚之義也。

translations.literal: Jizi missioned to Huaxia—also bore meaning of banquet converse.
translations.idiomatic: Jizi chatted at Zhou feasts—canonical parallel.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，欲知其君，觀其所使，見其下之明明，知其上之赫赫。

translations.literal: The ancients said: wish to know your lord—observe whom he sends—seeing clarity below—knows brilliance above.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys mirror kings.

sentences.zh: 溫若譽禮，能使彼歎之，誠所以昭我臣之多良，明使之得其人，顯國美於異境，揚君命於他邦。

translations.literal: If Wen praised Li—made them sigh admiration—indeed manifest our ministers' abundance of worth—proved envoy matched the man—displayed state beauty in foreign soil—raised lord mandate in other kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's praise advertised Wu's bench.

sentences.zh: 是以晉趙文子之盟於宋也，稱隨今於屈建。

translations.literal: Therefore when Zhao Wenzi of Jin covenanted at Song—he praised minister Sui before Qu Jian of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: At the Song league Zhao Wenzi touted Jin's minister Sui to Chu's Qu Jian—a classic compliment.

sentences.zh: 楚王孫圉之使於晉也，譽左史於趙鞅。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Chu's mission to Jin—praised the Left Scribe to Zhao Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's Sun Wei praised Zuo Shi before Zhao Yang in Jin.

sentences.zh: 亦向他國之輔，而歎本邦之臣，經傳美之以光國，而不譏之以外交也。

translations.literal: Thus sighing native ministers before another state's aides—classics bless this to brighten state—do not fault as illicit diplomacy.
translations.idiomatic: Annals applaud such praise—not treason.

sentences.zh: 王靖內不憂時，外不趨事，溫彈之不私，推之不假，於是與靖遂為大怨，此其盡節之明驗也。

translations.literal: Wang Jing inwardly fretted not the hour—outwardly rushed not affairs—Wen impeached him without private skew—pressed without indulgence—thereby Wang Jing nursed great grievance—this proves exhaustive loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's clash with Wang Jing proved impartial zeal.

sentences.zh: 靖兵眾之勢，干任之用，皆勝於賈原、蔣康，溫尚不容私以安於靖，豈敢賣恩以協原、康邪？

translations.literal: Jing's troop strength and commissioned weight—both surpassed Jia Yuan and Jiang Kang—Wen still refused private ease toward Jing—how dare sell grace to aid Yuan and Kang?
translations.idiomatic: If Wen snubbed mighty Jing he hardly horse-traded two petty clerks.

sentences.zh: 又原在職不勤，當事不堪，溫數對以丑色，彈以急聲。

translations.literal: Moreover Yuan—slack in office—could not bear duty—Wen repeatedly answered with ugly face—snapped urgent tone.
translations.idiomatic: Wen browbeat idle Jia Yuan—hardly courting him.

sentences.zh: 若其誠欲賣恩作亂，則亦不必貪原也。

translations.literal: If truly wishing sell grace and stir rebellion—need not covet Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Plotters would not bother with Yuan.

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，校之於事既不合，參之於眾亦不驗。

translations.literal: All these several points—checked against facts—do not align—cross-checked with crowd—not verified.
translations.idiomatic: Charges fail fact and gossip.

sentences.zh: 臣竊念人君雖有聖哲之姿，非常之智，然以一人之身御兆民之眾，從層宮之內，瞰四國之外，昭群下之情，求萬機之理，猶未易周也，固當聽察群下之言，以廣聰明之烈。

translations.literal: Your servant privately reflects: though a lord possess sage-wise bearing and extraordinary wit—yet with one body ruling myriad masses—from layered palace—overlooking four kingdoms—clarifying subordinates' hearts—seeking myriad threads' pattern—still not easy to compass fully—surely ought heed crowd speech—to widen keen hearing's blaze.
translations.idiomatic: One man atop a layered palace cannot alone sound every heart beyond the four seas or master every thread of policy—so he must weigh counsel from below and widen what his ears can hear.

sentences.zh: 今者人非溫既殷勤，臣是溫又契闊，辭則俱巧，意則俱至，各自言欲為國，誰其言欲為私，倉卒之間，猶難即別。

translations.literal: Now men opposing Wen speak fervently—your servant supporting Wen speaks earnest—both rhetoric clever—both intent arriving—each claims state motive—who admits private aim—in sudden moment—hard instantly to separate.
translations.idiomatic: Accusers and defender both sound patriotic.

sentences.zh: 然以殿下之聰睿，察講論之曲直。

translations.literal: Yet by Your Highness' perspicacity—examine debate's crooked straight.
translations.idiomatic: Quan can weigh bent from true.

sentences.zh: 若潛神留思，纖粗研核，情何嫌而不宣，事何昧而不昭哉?溫非親臣，臣非愛溫者也，昔之君子，皆抑私忿，以增君明。

translations.literal: If sink spirit—linger thought—fine and coarse scrutinize—what feeling stays hidden—what affair stays dark? Wen is no intimate minister—your servant no lover of Wen—former gentlemen all suppressed private wrath—to augment lord clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Tong claims no kinship—only duty like ancient advisors.

sentences.zh: 彼獨行之於前，臣恥廢之於後，故遂發宿懷於今日。

translations.literal: They walked thus before—your servant shames to abandon after—therefore vent long-held breast today.
translations.idiomatic: Their example forces Tong's memo.

sentences.zh: 納愚言於聖聽，實盡心於明朝，非有念於溫身也。

translations.literal: Submit foolish words to sacred hearing—truly exhaust heart for enlightened court—not from thought for Wen's person.
translations.idiomatic: The plea serves Wu—not Wen's skin.

sentences.zh: 權終不納。

translations.literal: Quan in the end did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Quan ignored him.

sentences.zh: 後六年，溫病卒。

translations.literal: Six years later Wen died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Six years on Wen died sick.

sentences.zh: 二弟祗、白，亦有才名，與溫俱廢。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Zhi and Bai—also bore talent's name—with Wen alike dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers Zhi and Bai fell with him.

sentences.zh: 〈《会稽典录》曰：餘姚虞俊叹曰：“张惠恕才多智少，华而不实，怨之所聚，有覆家之祸，吾见其兆矣。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dianlu states: Yu Jun of Yuyao sighed: "Zhang Huishu—much talent little wit—flowery yet hollow—resentment gathers—there lies overturn-house calamity—I see its portent.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun called Wen flashy fuel for ruin.

sentences.zh: ”诸葛亮闻俊忧温，意未之信，及温放黜，亮乃叹俊之有先见。

translations.literal: " Zhuge Liang hearing Jun's worry about Wen—intent did not yet believe—once Wen was cashiered—Liang then sighed Jun had foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Kongming doubted until Wen fell—then praised Yu Jun.

sentences.zh: 亮初闻温败，未知其故，思之数日，曰：“吾已得之矣，其人於清浊太明，善恶太分。

translations.literal: Liang first hearing Wen's ruin—not knowing cause—pondered several days—said: "I have got it—this man on purity and turbidity too bright—good and evil too sharply split.
translations.idiomatic: Liang judged Wen too harsh a moralist.

sentences.zh: ”臣松之以为庄周云“名者公器也，不可以多取”，张温之废，岂其取名之多乎！

translations.literal: " Your servant Songzhi considers Zhuang Zhou said "fame is public vessel—not to be grasped excessively"—Zhang Wen's dismissal—could it be from grasping fame too much!
translations.idiomatic: Pei cites Zhuangzi—fame devoured Wen.

sentences.zh: 多之为弊，古贤既知之矣。

translations.literal: That excess becomes flaw—ancient worthies already knew.
translations.idiomatic: Sages warned against hunger for name.

sentences.zh: 是以远见之士，退藏於密，不使名浮於德，不以华伤其实，既不能被褐韫宝，挫廉逃誉，使才映一世，声盖人上，冲用之道，庸可暂替！

translations.literal: Therefore far-seeing gentlemen hide deep in secrecy—not letting fame float above virtue—not letting blossom wound kernel—cannot don coarse robe concealing treasure—still humble virtue fleeing praise—yet causing talent to shine one age—voice topping mankind—such humility's way—how endure brief substitution!
translations.idiomatic: Far-sighted men therefore bury themselves from acclaim—never letting renown outrun virtue or blossom eclipse kernel—and though few can wrap treasure in sackcloth and flee praise entirely, those who flash talent across an age while topping every tongue abandon the low-profile Way; that temper cannot hold long.

sentences.zh: 温则反之，能无败乎？

translations.literal: Wen reversed this—could he avoid defeat?
translations.idiomatic: Wen did opposite—fall followed.

sentences.zh: 权既疾温名盛，而骆统方骤言其美，至云“卓跞冠群，炜晔曜世，世人未有及之者也”。

translations.literal: Quan already resented Wen's swelling fame—while Luo Tong suddenly praised his beauty—even saying "towering above the crowd—blazing through the age—none among contemporaries matched him."
translations.idiomatic: Quan hated Wen's renown while Tong crowned him peerless—oil on flame.

sentences.zh: 斯何异燎之方盛，又捴膏以炽之哉！

translations.literal: How differs from blaze already roaring—then ladling fat to feed it!
translations.idiomatic: Like pouring lard on bonfire.

sentences.zh: 《文士传》曰：温姊妹三人皆有节行，为温事，已嫁者皆见录夺。

translations.literal: The Anthology of Literati states: Wen's three sisters—all possessed integrity—because of Wen affair—those already married were all seized and stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's fall dragged three married sisters.

sentences.zh: 其中妹先適顾承，官以许嫁丁氏，成婚有日，遂饮药而死。

translations.literal: The middle sister had married Gu Cheng—the officialhouse pledged her to Ding clan—wedding day approaching—she drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: One sister poisoned herself rather than remarry Ding.

sentences.zh: 吴朝嘉叹，乡人图画，为之赞颂云。〉

translations.literal: Wu court praised and sighed—home villagers painted images—for them hymn of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wu canonized her—village murals sang her.

sentences.zh: 駱統字公緒，會稽烏傷人也。

translations.literal: Luo Tong, courtesy name Gongxu, was a man of Wushang in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong, styled Gongxu, from Wushang.

sentences.zh: 父俊，官至陳相。

translations.literal: His father Jun rose to Chancellor of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Father Jun reached Chen chancellor.

sentences.zh: 為袁術所害。

translations.literal: Was murdered by Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu killed him.

sentences.zh: 〈谢承后汉书曰：俊字孝远，有文武才幹，少为郡吏，察孝廉，补尚书郎，擢拜陈相。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng's Later Han History states: Jun, courtesy name Xiaoyuan, possessed civil and martial talent—in youth served as commandery clerk—nominated Flourishing Talent—filled vacancy Court Gentleman—promoted Chancellor of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Jun—styled Xiaoyuan—rose from clerk to Chen.

sentences.zh: 值袁术僭号，兄弟忿争，天下鼎沸，群贼并起，陈与比界，奸慝四布，俊厉威武，保疆境，贼不敢犯。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shu usurped title—brothers quarreled—all under Heaven boiled—bandits rose together—Chen bordered him—wickedness spread four ways—Jun hardened martial awe—guarded frontier—bandits dared not strike.
translations.idiomatic: Jun shielded Chen when Shu seized imperial style.

sentences.zh: 养济百姓，灾害不生，岁获丰稔。

translations.literal: He nourished and aided hundred surnames—disaster did not arise—years harvested abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen flourished under his care.

sentences.zh: 后术军众饥困，就俊求粮。

translations.literal: Later Shu's army multitude hungered and distressed—approached Jun seeking grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's starving host begged Chen grain.

sentences.zh: 俊疾恶术，初不应答。

translations.literal: Jun hated Shu's wickedness—at first gave no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused the tyrant.

sentences.zh: 术怒，密使人杀俊。〉

translations.literal: Shu angry—secretly sent men kill Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Shu assassinated him.

sentences.zh: 統母改適，為華歆小妻，統時八歲，遂與親客歸會稽。

translations.literal: Tong's mother remarried—as concubine of Hua Xin—Tong then eight sui—thereupon with kin retainers returned to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he quit stepfather Hua Xin for Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 其母送之，拜辭上車，面而不顧，其母泣涕於後。

translations.literal: His mother escorted him—he bowed farewell mounted carriage—face forward never looked back—his mother wept tears behind.
translations.idiomatic: He rode off without looking—mother wept.

sentences.zh: 御者曰：「夫人猶在也。

translations.literal: Charioteer said: "Your mother still stands there.
translations.idiomatic: The driver said mother still watched.

sentences.zh: 」統曰：「不欲增母思，故不顧耳。

translations.literal: " Tong said: "I wish not increase mother's longing—therefore do not look back.
translations.idiomatic: Tong feared backward glance would wound her more.

sentences.zh: 」事適母甚謹。

translations.literal: " He served stepmother most scrupulously.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his stepmother strictly.

sentences.zh: 時饑荒，鄉里及遠方客多有困乏，統為之飲食衰少。

translations.literal: Times famine—hamlet and distant guests many distressed—Tong for their sake drank and ate less.
translations.idiomatic: Famine years saw him fast for neighbors.

sentences.zh: 其姊仁愛有行，寡歸無子，見統甚哀之，數問其故。

translations.literal: His elder sister benevolent and loving with conduct—widowed returned childless—seeing Tong deeply pitied him—often asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: His widowed sister pressed why he starved.

sentences.zh: 統曰：「士大夫糟糠不足，我何心獨飽!」姊曰：「誠如是，何不告我，而自苦若此？

translations.literal: Tong said: "Gentlemen lack even chaff coarse grain—what heart have I to feast alone!" Sister said: "If truly so—why not tell me—and bitter yourself thus?
translations.idiomatic: He said scholars starved—how could he feast? She begged him to speak.

sentences.zh: 」乃自以私粟與統，又以告母，母亦賢之，遂使分施，由是顯名。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she privately gave Tong grain from own stores—also told mother—mother likewise deemed worthy—thereupon ordered divide and distribute—thereby fame appeared.
translations.idiomatic: She fed him from private bins—mother approved—fame spread.

sentences.zh: 孫權以將軍領會稽太守，統年二十，試為烏程相，民戶過萬，咸歎其惠理。

translations.literal: Sun Quan as general concurrent Administrator of Kuaiji—Tong twenty sui—trial appointment magistrate of Wucheng—households exceeding ten thousand—all sighed his kindly governance.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he governed ten thousand Wucheng households.

sentences.zh: 權嘉之，召為功曹，行騎都尉，妻以從兄輔女。

translations.literal: Quan praised him—summoned Clerk of Merit—acting Commandant of Cavalry—married him to cousin Fu's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Quan made him Clerk of Merit and Fu's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 統志在補察，苟所聞見，夕不待旦。

translations.literal: Tong's ambition lay remedying oversight—whatever heard or seen—evening waited not dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed fault reports overnight.

sentences.zh: 常勸權以尊賢接士，勤求損益，饗賜之日，可人人別進。

translations.literal: Often urged Quan honor worthies receive gentlemen—diligently seek gain and loss—on feast grant days—might enter each man separately.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Quan to toast ministers one by one.

sentences.zh: 問其燥溼，加以密意，誘諭使言，察其志趣，令皆感恩戴義，懷欲報之心。

translations.literal: Ask dry or damp—add confidential kindness—coax speech—observe bent of will—make each grateful bearing duty—harbor wish to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Probe hardship—win loyalty.

sentences.zh: 權納用焉。

translations.literal: Quan adopted and used it.
translations.idiomatic: Quan listened.

sentences.zh: 出為建忠中郎將，領武射吏三千人。

translations.literal: He went out General Who Establishes Loyalty—commanding three thousand archer guards.
translations.idiomatic: He led three thousand picked bowmen.

sentences.zh: 及淩統死，復領其兵。

translations.literal: When Ling Tong died—again commanded his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Ling Tong's column.

sentences.zh: 是時徵役繁數，重以疫癘，民戶損耗，統上疏曰：

translations.literal: At this time levies and corvée piled thick—heavy with plague—households wasted away—Tong submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Plague and drafts gutted the south—Tong wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞君國者，以據疆土為彊富，制威福為尊貴，曜德義為榮顯，永世胤為豐祚。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: he who rules a state—holds territory strong and rich—wields blessing and awe noble—displays virtue and righteousness glorious—extends generations heir fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Realm needs land, awe, virtue, heirs.

sentences.zh: 然財須民生，彊賴民力，威恃民勢，福由民殖，德俟民茂，義以民行，六者既備，然後應天受祚，保族宜邦。

translations.literal: Yet wealth needs people's life—strength relies people's force—awe depends people's momentum—blessing grows from people's increase—virtue awaits people's flourishing—righteousness by people practiced—these six prepared—then answer Heaven receiving mandate—protect clan fitting state.
translations.idiomatic: All six roots feed from the people.

sentences.zh: 書曰：『衆非后無能胥以寧，后非衆無以辟四方。

translations.literal: Documents states: 'Multitude without lord cannot together be tranquil—lord without multitude cannot open four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Classic bonds lord and folk.

sentences.zh: 』推是言之，則民以君安，君以民濟，不易之道也。

translations.literal: ' Pushing this saying—people secure because of lord—lord aided because of people—unchanging way.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ruled need each other.

sentences.zh: 今彊敵未殄，海內未乂，三軍有無已之役，江境有不釋之備，徵賦調數，由來積紀，加以殃疫死喪之災，郡縣荒虛，田疇蕪曠，聽聞屬城，民戶浸寡，又多殘老，少有丁夫，聞此之日，心若焚燎。

translations.literal: Now mighty foe not extinguished—within seas not pacified—three armies endless campaigns—river frontier unslackened guard—levies and allocations repeated—inherited many years—added plague death mourning disasters—commanderies counties waste empty—fields wilderness vast—hearing dependent towns—households gradually few—also many crippled aged—few prime husbands—hearing this day—heart like burning pyre.
translations.idiomatic: War, tax, plague emptied Wu's farms of young men.

sentences.zh: 思尋所由，小民無知，既有安土重遷之性，且又前後出為兵者，生則困苦無有溫飽，死則委棄骸骨不反，是以尤用戀本畏遠，同之於死。

translations.literal: Thinking trace cause—petty folk unknowing—already possess nature loving soil dreading removal—and moreover those front and rear going out as soldiers—living then hardship lacking warmth full belly—dying then bones cast never returning—therefore doubly cling native soil fear distant—as toward death.
translations.idiomatic: Draft terror chains folk to home like fear of dying.

sentences.zh: 每有徵發，羸謹居家重累者先見輸送。

translations.literal: Whenever levy issued—weak prudent households heavy burdened—appear first for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Caretakers ship sons first.

sentences.zh: 小有財貨，傾居行賂，不顧窮盡。

translations.literal: Those with slight wealth—empty dwelling bribing—heedless exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Rich buy exemptions until broke.

sentences.zh: 輕剽者則迸入險阻，黨就羣惡。

translations.literal: Light rash ones—bolt into peril—gang with wicked packs.
translations.idiomatic: Bold ones flee to bandits.

sentences.zh: 百姓虛竭，嗷然愁擾，愁擾則不營業，不營業則致窮困，致窮困則不樂生，故口腹急，則姦心動而攜叛多也。

translations.literal: Hundred surnames emptied—howling troubled—troubled then no livelihood—no livelihood brings extreme want—extreme want unhappy living—therefore belly urgent—then wicked hearts stir and desertion alliance multiplies.
translations.idiomatic: When households are drained and voices rise in distress, fields lie idle, poverty bites, and life loses savor—bellies grow desperate, wicked intent stirs, and desertion spreads.

sentences.zh: 又聞民閒，非居處小能自供，生產兒子，多不起養；

translations.literal: Moreover hearing among the people—unless dwelling slight ability self-supplies—bearing sons—they often fail to raise them;
translations.idiomatic: Common folk too poor to feed newborns abandoned infants.

sentences.zh: 屯田貧兵，亦多棄子。

translations.literal: Garrison troops’ poor soldiers—also many abandon children.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier colonists dumped babies too.

sentences.zh: 天則生之，而父母殺之，既懼干逆和氣，感動陰陽。

translations.literal: Heaven then bore them—yet parents kill them—already fearing offense against harmonious qi—moving yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends life while parents end it—such slaughter twists cosmic balance.

sentences.zh: 且惟殿下開基建國，乃無窮之業也，彊鄰大敵非造次所滅，疆埸常守非期月之戍，而兵民減耗，後生不育，非所以歷遠年，致成功也。

translations.literal: Moreover only Your Highness opens foundation building state—yet enterprise without end—strong neighbor great foe not destroyed in haste—border guard constant—not one month’s garrison—yet soldiers and people shrink—later births not nurtured—not the means to span distant years and achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: Wu faces endless wars yet loses breeders—no dynasty survives that.

sentences.zh: 夫國之有民，猶水之有舟，停則以安，擾則以危，愚而不可欺，弱而不可勝，是以聖王重焉，禍福由之，故與民消息，觀時制政。

translations.literal: Now a state possessing people—like water possessing boat—still then peace—troubled then peril—foolish yet not deceiveable—weak yet not conquerable—therefore sage kings weigh them—blessing and disaster follow—thus with people exhale and inhale—observe times shaping policy.
translations.idiomatic: People are the hull—still water floats the ship; chop the waves and it founders.

sentences.zh: 方今長吏親民之職，惟以辨具為能，取過目前之急，少復以恩惠為治，副稱殿下天覆之仁，勤恤之德者。

translations.literal: Today chief clerks’ posts cherishing people—only regard sorting gear as ability—grasp passing urgent trouble ahead—little again treat gracious kindness as governance—matching Your Highness Heaven-covering benevolence—diligent pitying virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates chase quotas, not mercy—betraying your humane rule.

sentences.zh: 官民政俗，日以彫弊，漸以陵遲，勢不可久。

translations.literal: Official manner people custom—daily carve decay—gradually slope decline—momentum cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Administration and folkways rot—collapse looms.

sentences.zh: 夫治疾及其未篤，除患貴其未深，願殿下少以萬機餘閒，留神思省，補復荒虛，深圖遠計，育殘餘之民，阜人財之用，參曜三光，等崇天地。

translations.literal: Now treating illness reach before grave—removing disaster treasure before deep—pray Your Highness slightly from myriad threads’ leftover leisure—linger spirit ponder inspect—repair restore waste emptiness—deep plot distant plan—nurture surviving people—enrich human wealth’s use—triplicate blaze three luminaries—equal honor Heaven Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Heal before terminal ruin—spare thought for hollow counties and starved farms.

sentences.zh: 臣統之大願，足以死而不朽矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Tong’s great wish—suffices die yet imperishable.
translations.idiomatic: To serve thus would immortalize Tong’s death.

sentences.zh: 權感統言，深加意焉。

translations.literal: Quan was moved by Tong’s words—deeply attended them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan took the memorial to heart.

sentences.zh: 以隨陸遜破蜀軍於宜都，遷偏將軍。

translations.literal: For following Lu Xun defeating Shu army at Yidu—promoted Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu victory beside Lu Xun won him stars.

sentences.zh: 黃武初，曹仁攻濡須，使別將常雕等襲中洲，統與嚴圭共拒破之，封新陽亭侯，後為濡須督。

translations.literal: Huangwu early—Cao Ren attacked Ruxu—sent separate general Chang Diao and others raid Middle Isle—Tong with Yan Gui jointly resisted and broke them—ennobled Marquis of Xinyang village—later became Ruxu commander.
translations.idiomatic: He repelled Cao Ren’s raid at Ruxu and held the ford.

sentences.zh: 數陳便宜，前後書數十上，所言皆善，文多故不悉載。

translations.literal: Repeatedly presented convenience proposals—front and rear memorials dozens submitted—speech all good—text lengthy therefore not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Scores of sound memorials go uncopied here.

sentences.zh: 尤以占募在民閒長惡敗俗，生離叛之心，急宜絕置，權與相反覆，終遂行之。

translations.literal: Especially deemed recruiting levies among people lengthened evil ruined custom—bred separation rebellious hearts—urgently ought cease establish—Quan with him debated back and forth—in end followed through.
translations.idiomatic: He condemned mercenary drafts corrupting morals—Quan yielded after debate.

sentences.zh: 年三十六，黃武七年卒。

translations.literal: Age thirty-six—Huangwu seventh year died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six in Huangwu 7.

translations.idiomatic: Chiwu 9 made him agile cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 遭二宮構爭，據擁護太子，言則懇至，義形於色，守之以死，

translations.literal: Met two-palace structure struggle—Ju embraced protected heir apparent—speech then earnest utmost—righteousness shaped face—guarded with death—
translations.idiomatic: He defended the crown prince unto death—

sentences.zh: 〈殷基《通语》载据争曰：“臣闻太子国之本根，雅性仁孝，天下归心，今卒责之，将有一朝之虑。

translations.literal: Yin Ji Tongyu records Ju disputed: "Your servant hears heir apparent state root trunk—refined nature benevolent filial—all under Heaven return heart—now suddenly blame him—will have morning's worry.
translations.idiomatic: Tongyu cites Ju’s warning—the heir is the root.

sentences.zh: 昔晋献用骊姬而申生不存，汉武信江充而戾太子冤死。

translations.literal: Formerly Jin Xian used Li Ji then Shensheng not preserved—Han Wu trusted Jiang Chong then Crown Prince Li unjust died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji and Jiang Chong lessons.

sentences.zh: 臣窃惧太子不堪其忧，虽立思子之宫，无所复及矣。”〉

translations.literal: Your servant privately fears heir cannot bear that worry—though erect Son-Remembering palace—nothing again reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Even a repentant hall cannot recall dead heir.

sentences.zh: 遂左遷新都郡丞。

translations.literal: Thereupon demoted left Administrator Assistant Xindu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Quan banished him Xindu assistant.

sentences.zh: 未到，中書令孫弘譖潤據，因權寢疾，弘為詔書追賜死，時年五十七。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Palace Secretariat Director Sun Hong slandered Zhu Ju with soaking malice; because Quan lay gravely ill, Hong forged an edict commanding him to commit suicide—he was fifty-seven sui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hong whispered poison into a dying Quan's ear and forged an order—Ju never reached his post; they forced him to die at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 孫亮時，二子熊、損各復領兵，為全公主所謂，皆死。

translations.literal: Under Sun Liang his two sons Xiong and Sun each again commanded troops—slandered by the Princess of Quan—both died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang restored both sons to commands; Princess Quan framed them and both perished.

sentences.zh: 永安中，迫錄前功，以熊子宣襲爵雲陽侯，尚公主。

translations.literal: During Yong'an they posthumously tallied former merit—Xiong's son Xuan inherited the Marquisate of Yunyang and married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an auditors remembered old service—Xuan took the Yunyang title and a princess bride.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，宣至驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Under Sun Hao Xuan rose to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hao he climbed to agile cavalry command.

translations.literal: [Appraisal]
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：虞翻古之狂直，因難免乎末世，然權不能容，非曠宇也。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Yu Fan was blunt straightness in the ancient mold—thereby hard to escape harm in a degenerate age—yet that Quan could not tolerate him shows no spacious breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou calls Fan a classical blunt loyalist ill-suited to a fallen age—yet Quan's inability to shelter him betrays a petty court.

sentences.zh: 陸績之於揚《玄》，是仲尼之左丘明，老聘之嚴周矣；

translations.literal: Lu Ji toward Yang Xiong's Mystery parallels Confucius having Zuo Qiuming and Laozi having Zhuang Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji stood to Yang Xiong's Taixuan as Confucius to Zuo Qiu or Laozi to Zhuang Zhou—a peer interpreter.

sentences.zh: 以瑚璉之器，而作守南越，不亦賊夫人歟！

translations.literal: With talents fit for ritual vessels—yet made guardian of southern Yue—is it not wasting the man!
translations.idiomatic: Temple-grade talent parked on a Ling frontier—what misuse of a man!

sentences.zh: 張溫才藻俊茂，而智防未備，用致艱患。

translations.literal: Zhang Wen's literary brilliance flourished lush—yet wisdom's defenses were not prepared—thereby inviting bitter calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen blazed with letters but lacked political guardrails—and paid for it.

sentences.zh: 駱統抗明大義，辭切理至，值權方閉不開。

translations.literal: Luo Tong upheld and clarified great righteousness—speech cutting, principle utmost—yet met Quan sealed shut and unopening.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong framed the grand moral case with knife-edge clarity—against Quan's deaf door.

sentences.zh: 陸瑁篤義規諫，君子有稱焉。

translations.literal: Lu Mao was steadfast in righteousness and remonstrance—gentlemen have praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mao's loyal counsel earned gentlemen's praise.

sentences.zh: 吾粲、朱據遭罹屯蹇，以正喪身，悲夫！

translations.literal: Wu Can and Zhu Ju encountered hardship and obstruction—through upright principle lost their lives—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Can and Zhu Ju died for doing right—grief on grief.
